Memory is now machine-readable at both the collection and single-entry level.

cards.title: Profile files as JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse user show --json and niuse identity show --json emit {path, text}.
  • A missing file is text: null, not an empty string; the path is always present.
  • Text output is unchanged.
  • An end-to-end test checks both commands on an empty home.

Acceptance

  • Both objects parse and carry an absolute path.
  • Missing text is null.
  • Text views are unchanged.
  • No storage change.

Notes

The two human-authored layers now have the same machine-readable shape as memory and journal.

cards.title: One-command dogfood row
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • scripts/dogfood.sh "note" reads niuse stats --days 1 --json and inserts today's row into docs/dogfood.md.
  • The date comes from the local calendar, matching journal and memory.
  • Running it twice in one day replaces the row instead of duplicating it; the YYYY-MM-DD placeholder is removed.
  • --file supports a scratch copy; NIUSE_BIN / NIUSE_HOME select the binary and store.
  • The guide explains that this records real use, not a reconstruction.

Acceptance

  • First run inserts one row and removes the placeholder.
  • Second run replaces the same-day row; the count stays one.
  • Notes are pipe-escaped.
  • An end-to-end shell test in scripts/check.sh covers one row, replacement, and no duplicate.
  • The script fails clearly when niuse is missing or the table is not found.

Notes

The command only formats numbers that already exist; it cannot make a day count. The ten real days are still the gate.

cards.title: Stats windows follow local calendar days
cards.body_html:
Problem

After day labels moved to the local calendar, stats --days 1 still used a rolling now - 24h cutoff. At 09:00 local it could show yesterday evening plus today, while claiming a one-day window; the labels and the window disagreed.

Fix

  • Date::start_millis_local returns local midnight for a calendar date, using the earliest valid instant across DST transitions.
  • window_start(days) is 0 for all time, otherwise local midnight days - 1 days ago.
  • stats and stats --trend share that cutoff.
  • Tests cover the local-midnight round trip and the one-day/two-day window starts; the CLI help says "local calendar days".

Acceptance

  • --days 1 starts at local midnight today.
  • --days 2 starts at local midnight yesterday.
  • --days 0 still means all time.
  • A DST transition cannot silently shift the cutoff by a day.
  • If a zone skips local midnight, the first valid hour is used instead of zero.

Notes

A day label and a day window should agree; otherwise the trend looks like it has data from a day it filtered out.

cards.title: identity.md is the only name source
cards.body_html:
问题

用户问「你是谁」，真实 REPL 答「我是 niuse」，被纠正后才改口。根因是 persona 的 BASE 硬编码了「你是 niuse」，而 identity.md 只是后面的一节；模型把产品名当成了自己的名字。

修复

  • BASE 不再自称名字，只描述工作方式，并明确「名字、语气与边界由后面的『你是谁』一节定义；产品名不是你的名字」。
  • identity 节增加「唯一真源」优先级：与本 prompt 其他段落（包括产品名）冲突时，以 identity 为准。
  • 协议段把「niuse 会解析」改成「运行时会解析」，减少产品名被当作人格线索。
  • identity 缺失时注入明确说明：尚未命名，不要用产品名充数，建议运行 niuse identity init。
  • 新增测试 identity_is_the_only_name_source 与 no_identity_does_not_invent_a_name。

验收

  • BASE 不再包含「你是 niuse」。
  • identity 节声明唯一真源。
  • 真实模型在 identity 写 niubot 时直接答「我是 niubot」，无需纠正。
  • 真实模型在 identity 缺失时只回一句「我还没有名字」，不跑工具、不自报 niuse；两次独立运行一致。
  • 现有 prompt 顺序与预算测试不变。

备注

产品名仍然出现在启动 banner、命令和文档里；它只是项目名，不是人格。identity 缺失时 persona 也不自报一个假名字。

cards.title: Dogfood progress in doctor
cards.body_html:
Problem

The M2 ten-day gate lived only in docs/dogfood.md. A user running the product had no signal of how many real days were recorded, so the state was easy to lose track of.

Scope

  • Count distinct local dates with turn metrics.
  • niuse doctor reports dogfood: N active day(s), warn under ten, ok at ten.
  • --json includes the same check.
  • No new store and no fabricated day: metrics count active days, not reviews.

Acceptance

  • Two turns on one day count once.
  • Turns on two days count twice.
  • Non-turn metrics do not count.
  • Under ten is a warning; ten or more is ok.
  • The check is present in text and JSON.
  • The docs say it is a proxy, not the acceptance review.

Notes

Ten active days do not close M2; the notes and acceptance trend still decide.

cards.title: Dogfood log validator
cards.body_html:
Problem

The M2 close condition is a table in a Markdown file. Structural mistakes (duplicate day, future date, accepted > proposed) and missing criteria could be read as completion.

Scope

  • Parse the dogfood table; reject malformed cells, bad dates, duplicates, future days, negative counts, and accepted > proposed.
  • Report days, aggregate acceptance, cited memory ids, and disagreements.
  • Default mode reports gaps and exits 0 for an in-progress log.
  • --complete exits non-zero until ten days, ≥60% acceptance, three cited ids, and one disagreement exist.
  • Deterministic self-test with partial, complete, duplicate, over-count, and future fixtures.

Acceptance

  • A one-row log reports 1/10 and exits 0.
  • The same log fails --complete.
  • A valid ten-row log passes --complete.
  • Duplicate, accepted > proposed, and future rows fail.
  • check.sh runs the live check and self-test.
  • The docs call the citation/disagreement counts heuristics.

Notes

The validator cannot judge whether a day was real; it only stops arithmetic and structure from lying. Human review remains the gate.

cards.title: Dogfood row command
cards.body_html:
Problem

The daily row required copying numbers from stats into Markdown by hand. That invites arithmetic mistakes and makes the ritual heavier than it needs to be.

Scope

  • niuse dogfood --file PATH --note TEXT [--json].
  • Read today's turn / propose / accept metrics.
  • Replace the same-date row or append a new one; never duplicate.
  • Refuse a note that looks like a secret.
  • New files are private; existing repo files keep their mode.
  • The wrapper script calls the binary so there is one update implementation.

Acceptance

  • The row uses today's metrics, not values passed by the user.
  • A second run replaces the same date.
  • Other rows and surrounding text are preserved.
  • A missing table is an error, not a silent append.
  • --json reports the row and file.
  • The wrapper delegates to the binary.

Notes

This writes a Markdown log, not a new durable store. The default path is ~/.niuse/dogfood.md; the project gate explicitly passes docs/dogfood.md.

cards.title: Weekly review report
cards.body_html:
Problem

The weekly review needed three commands: stats, doctor, and a manual read of the dogfood table. The numbers were individually correct but never assembled.

Scope

  • niuse report [--days N] [--dogfood PATH] [--json].
  • Combine window turns/errors, acceptance, tokens/cache, open goals/loops/plan, and dogfood days/acceptance.
  • Default the dogfood path to docs/dogfood.md when it exists.
  • Read-only; no new store.

Acceptance

  • Metrics produce turns, errors, acceptance, cache hit, tokens/turn.
  • Store counts produce open goals, promises (with overdue), plan steps.
  • Dogfood rows produce days and aggregate acceptance.
  • docs/dogfood.md is used when present.
  • --json is stable for scripts.
  • Text output is a compact Markdown-ready block.

Notes

This is a review aid, not the M2 gate. The validator and human notes still decide.

cards.title: Weekly report in REPL and TUI
cards.body_html:
Problem

niuse report existed only as a subcommand. The weekly review is most useful where the work happens, without leaving the session.

Scope

  • Shared report_text used by CLI, REPL, and TUI.
  • REPL /report [days], default 7.
  • TUI /report, default 7 and cwd/docs/dogfood.md when present.
  • Add both to help/completion.

Acceptance

  • REPL /report 14 parses the day window.
  • TUI /report returns the same report text.
  • The dogfood file is picked up from cwd/docs/dogfood.md.
  • Commands appear in help/completion.
  • No second implementation of the report.

Notes

The CLI remains the JSON surface; the in-session commands are text-only.

cards.title: Count distinct cited memories
cards.body_html:
Problem

dogfood-check.py counted one citation per row, not per distinct memory id. Ten days that all said m-abcd would satisfy the "3 citations" gate, while one day with three real ids would fail. The label already said "cited memory ids".

Scope

  • Collect m-xxxx ids across every note into a set.
  • Fail --complete when fewer than three distinct ids are cited.
  • Keep cited_memory_ids as a count; add cited_ids for the list.
  • A repeated-id fixture must fail; the complete fixture uses three ids.

Acceptance

  • Three distinct ids in one row count as three.
  • Ten rows repeating one id fail.
  • The self-test covers both cases.
  • The live table now reports 3 cited ids and only the 2/10 day gap.
  • M2-001's citation checkbox is satisfied.

Notes

Today's real retrieval cited m-f356, m-5c68, and m-3d0b; the first task cited two, the second listed all three. These are three different judgments, not one id repeated.

cards.title: Release and dependency strategy
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Decide the niucode dependency: publish niucode crates first, convert to pinned git revisions, or keep the two-checkout build.
  • Add license, repository, description, and other release metadata.
  • Make cargo package / cargo publish --dry-run reproducible.
  • Confirm crate-name availability; rename the crate if needed while keeping the niuse binary.

Acceptance

  • cargo package -p niuse passes against crates.io.
  • The install path is reproducible on a clean machine (cargo install niuse --version 0.1.12 --locked).
  • License and naming strategy are documented in the README and distribution doc.

Notes

Findings and options are recorded in distribution. 2026-10-22: the original crates are published, but niucode-mcp is not on crates.io, so cargo package -p niuse fails on that dependency. niucode-mcp now packages and passes cargo publish --dry-run; the publish order includes it. This card stays backlog until the authorized upload and a passing cargo package -p niuse.

2026-10-23: niucode-mcp 0.1.5 is published. The next blocker is the niuse version: crates.io core 0.1.11 predates the plan API. M3-006 prepares 0.1.12; core must be uploaded before the CLI package can verify.

2026-10-23: released. niuse/niuse-core 0.1.12 and niucode-* 0.1.6 are published; package verification and clean-root install pass. The first CLI upload failed on pack paths and the pre-EmbedderTool registry API; both are fixed and recorded in the release page.

cards.title: Distribution claims match the repository
cards.body_html:
Problem

docs/distribution.md claimed cargo install --git https://github.com/niuverse/niuse worked. A clean clone has no sibling niucode, and the path = "../niucode/..." dependencies cannot be fetched, so the command fails before building.

Evidence

  • Cloned the repository into /tmp and ran cargo metadata: failed to load manifest for dependency niucode-agent.
  • cargo install --path crates/niuse-cli --root /tmp/niuse-install --locked --debug from the two-checkout workspace installed a working niuse 0.1.0.

Fix

  • Document the two-checkout build and cargo install --path as what works.
  • Add a section proving why cargo install --git cannot work.
  • Replace the misleading options-table row with "keep the two-checkout build" and note that converting to git dependencies is a separate change.

Acceptance

  • No document claims cargo install --git works.
  • The clean-clone failure is quoted with the real error.
  • The working install path is verified and recorded.
  • crates.io blocking reason is unchanged and still accurate.

Notes

A distribution note that recommends a command which cannot work is worse than saying "not yet": it burns the reader's first five minutes and hides the real blocker.

cards.title: Niucode crates as versioned dependencies
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse's five niucode-* dependencies now carry version = "0.1.0" beside path.
  • Local development and the pinned checkout are unchanged.
  • niucode's internal dependencies are also versioned, and a publish-order script exists.
  • The remaining release prerequisites are a license and a crates.io token.

Acceptance

  • Workspace still builds and tests with path + version dependencies.
  • niucode crates share 0.1.0 and list the publish order.
  • niuse-core is also a versioned dependency of the binary.
  • Publish niucode-core and its dependents to crates.io (all seven at 0.1.0).
  • Verify cargo package -p niuse against the registry afterwards; it succeeds and the binary installs from crates.io.

cargo package -p niuse now gets past manifest validation and stops at the expected no matching package named niucode-agent until the registry upload exists.

Notes

This is the chosen distribution path: publish the kernel crates first, then the product. The two unchecked items require the user's license choice and token.

cards.title: Publish-state documentation
cards.body_html:
Problem

Status and distribution disagreed about the release state: status claimed cargo package -p niuse succeeded and mentioned 0.1.3/0.1.6, while distribution said packaging was blocked. The real state was mixed: 0.1.11 was published, but the new niucode-mcp dependency was not.

Scope

  • Check crates.io for niuse, niuse-core, niucode-*, niucode-mcp.
  • Run cargo package -p niuse --no-verify against the registry.
  • Correct the seven-store count in the status snapshot.
  • Record the exact blocker: niucode-mcp is unpublished.

Acceptance

  • Status says seven stores, not six.
  • Status no longer claims packaging succeeds.
  • Distribution names the real current blocker.
  • M3-001 remains backlog with the same blocker.
  • No version is bumped or published in this card.

Notes

Historical 0.1.3/0.1.6 install checks remain true for those versions; they are no longer presented as the current state.

2026-10-22 follow-up: niucode-mcp package and publish dry-run pass; the only blocker is the authorized upload.

cards.title: Prepare niuse 0.1.12
cards.body_html:
Problem

niucode-mcp 0.1.5 is published, but cargo package -p niuse still failed: crates.io niuse-core 0.1.11 predates the plan API. The workspace version was never bumped when PlanStep and compose_with_plan landed.

Scope

  • Bump the workspace and niuse-cli dependency to 0.1.12.
  • cargo package -p niuse-core passes at 0.1.12.
  • cargo package -p niuse resolves the registry core 0.1.12, so it needs that upload first.
  • No upload happens in this card.

Acceptance

  • Workspace and dependency are 0.1.12.
  • cargo check --workspace passes.
  • cargo package -p niuse-core passes.
  • niuse-core 0.1.12 is published.
  • cargo package -p niuse passes against the registry.

Notes

2026-10-23: core 0.1.12 and CLI 0.1.12 are published; package and clean-root install pass. The first CLI attempt exposed pack assets outside the crate and registry niucode 0.1.5 missing EmbedderTool; the release ships niucode 0.1.6 and embeds the packs under crates/niuse-cli/assets.

cards.title: 0.1.12 release runbook
cards.body_html:
Problem

The 0.1.12 upload is a human-authorized action with a strict order: core first, index wait, then the CLI. The exact commands and verification were spread across the distribution doc and the publish script.

Scope

  • One runbook with preflight evidence, commands, verification, and failure handling.
  • No upload in this card.
  • Record the dry-run result and the dogfood-trend “insufficient data” behavior.

Acceptance

  • The runbook names the authorization requirement.
  • Preflight evidence is dated and includes the core dry-run.
  • The core-first order and 20s index wait match the script.
  • Post-upload verification includes package and clean-root install.
  • Failure handling says bump, do not reuse.

Notes

This card changes no code. It exists so the authorized upload is a single reviewable step rather than an improvised sequence.

cards.title: Reuse niucode's TUI through a library and hooks
cards.blocked_reason: Renderer removal waits on ten real TUI dogfood days (M5-002) and ADR-0004.
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niucode-cli exposes a library target: session runtime, TUI entry, renderer, approval UI.
  • A small hook surface: augment the system prompt before a turn, observe a finished turn, receive session lifecycle events.
  • niuse implements the hooks: identity / memory injection, candidate extraction, journal and loop writes.
  • Delete niuse's renderer and its per-turn AgentConfig assembly once the shared path is stable.
  • Step 1 is done in niucode aac20a1: niucode-cli exports run(), TurnHooks, and NoHooks.
  • Step 2 is done for both entry points: the exec path invokes all three hooks through run_exec_with_hooks; the TUI path has TuiOptions / run_tui_with_hooks and invokes prompt, event, and turn-end through a shared hook cell. filter_text adds the streaming seam.
  • Renderer migration is analysed in M4-002; the files do not move until the confirmation and command seams exist.

Acceptance

  • A niuse binary runs niucode's TUI with memory injected and candidates confirmed.
  • niuse no longer owns a renderer or a second terminal input loop.
  • The hook trait is generic: no identity or memory types cross into niucode.
  • Contract tests still pass against the pinned revision.

Notes

This is the only large piece of duplication left. Keeping two repos is still the decision (ADR-0003); this card removes the reason the boundary felt wrong, without merging the products.

cards.title: Renderer migration gap analysis
cards.body_html:
范围

  • 对比 niuse render.rs（361 行）与 niucode TUI（约 3 960 行）的职责。
  • 确认已有 seam：augment_system_prompt、on_event、filter_text、on_turn_end。
  • filter_text 已实现并在 PTY 下验证：协议块可在显示前剥离，持久化事件不变。
  • 明确还缺的两个产品 seam：candidate 确认交互、embedder 命令注册。
  • 给出分阶段迁移计划，结论是不直接搬文件。

验收

  • 职责清单与代码规模量化。
  • 阻塞 gap 列清楚（确认、命令、审批、usage、config）。
  • filter_text 作为第一步落地并有运行时验证。
  • 迁移门槛写成十天 dogfood，不提前删除 renderer。

备注

详见 renderer-migration。去留已写成 ADR-0004：TUI 先 opt-in，十个真实狗粮日后再删 renderer。

cards.title: niuse CompanionHooks adapter
cards.body_html:
范围

  • 新增 tui feature，默认 niuse 二进制不依赖 niucode TUI。
  • CompanionHooks 实现 TurnHooks：
    • augment_system_prompt 注入 niuse 的 composed prompt；
    • filter_text 用 StreamFilter 剥离协议块，同时保留 raw 文本；
    • after_turn 自动写 journal/loops，把 memory 变成 accept/discard prompt；
    • on_answer 写 memory 或记录 discard。
  • 两个单元测试覆盖 accept 与 discard，且 loop 自动写入。
  • 已接 niuse tui（feature）并用 replay fixture 做 PTY 端到端：协议块被剥离、出现 accept/discard 问题、accept 后 memory 落盘。

验收

  • 默认构建不引入 TUI 依赖。
  • --features tui 测试与 clippy 通过。
  • 协议块剥离、journal/loop 自动写入、memory accept/replace/keep/discard 有测试。
  • 真正的 niuse tui 入口与 replay PTY 端到端测试。

cards.title: TUI approval and usage parity
cards.body_html:
Problem

niuse tui already runs the product hooks, but its approval presentation and usage line are niucode's defaults. The REPL contract is stricter: an 80-line preview, d for the full diff, denial returns the structured preview, and one session-level usage line feeds /cost. Until the two match, the renderer cannot be retired and the TUI cannot become the default.

Scope

  • Compare the approval path end to end: preview cap, full-diff action, denial payload, colour, and cancellation.
  • Compare usage accounting: per-run totals, /cost, cached tokens, and the compact line shown after a turn.
  • Make every product command reachable and discoverable in the TUI help and slash completion: /brief, /mem, /loops, /journal, /status, /cost, /export, /threads, /sessions, /prompt, /identity, /user.
  • Record the decision in renderer-migration.md; do not delete render.rs in this card.

Acceptance

  • A PTY test denies an approval with the configured y/n keys and asserts the write is blocked and the preview was visible.
  • /cost and the post-turn usage line agree with the event log.
  • Every listed product command appears in TUI help/completion and returns the same data as its REPL counterpart.
  • ./scripts/check.sh is green, including the tui feature.

Notes

The key conflict is resolved upstream: niucode 2d12360 adds TuiOptions.approval_keys, and niuse sets y/n/s. d no longer denies on the niuse path; the pager's full diff is always available with scrolling, so the 80-line cap is a REPL property, not a TUI requirement.

tests/tui_approval.py is the offline PTY proof: it sees the configured footer, checks that d is ignored, denies with n and confirms no file, then allows with y and confirms the write. /cost now reads the thread event log, the same source as the REPL, instead of accumulating a second total in the hook.

The renderer stays until M5-002 records ten real TUI days (ADR-0004).

If the gap is a niucode API issue, upstream it and bump the pin through scripts/sync-niucode.sh; do not fork the TUI.

cards.title: Ten TUI dogfood days
cards.body_html:
Problem

The TUI path passes synthetic PTY tests, but ADR-0004 requires ten real working days before the renderer can be removed or the TUI can become the default. Synthetic turns cannot reveal candidate fatigue, approval confusion, or terminal-specific rendering failures.

Scope

  • Use niuse tui for at least one real task on ten working days.
  • Record each day with ./scripts/dogfood.sh "note", including the task, the outcome, and one concrete memory win or disagreement.
  • Note every TUI-specific failure; do not round a partial day up.
  • Do not delete render.rs until the gate is complete.

Acceptance

  • Ten distinct working days are recorded, with at least one real task each.
  • At least three entries cite a past judgement correctly.
  • At least one entry records a disagreement with a reason.
  • The TUI path has no unresolved approval or data-loss failure.
  • The gate result is recorded in docs/dogfood.md and the ADR-0004 decision event.

Notes

2026-10-22: day 1/10. One real TUI turn replied 391 through the provider (13k input, 2 output). This is a recorded TUI day, not a synthetic replay.

2026-10-23: day 2/10. A real TUI task read DAY_TWO_C.md and answered with its heading (27k input, 47 output, 13.4k cached). The turn initially recorded 0 metrics; M5-010 added the missing on_turn_end. Eight distinct working days remain; the same calendar day cannot count twice.

If the gate fails, keep the REPL default and open a focused card for the failure instead of extending the gate's definition.

cards.title: Adopt the TUI's new session after /clear
cards.body_html:
Problem

A PTY test for /new exposed a session-path mismatch. Niucode's TUI /clear (or the new /new alias) calls new_session, which creates a timestamped file in the session directory and ends the old thread.jsonl. Niuse's CompanionHooks still holds thread.jsonl.

Consequences while the TUI runs:

  • /evidence reads the old thread.
  • /verify appends to the old thread.
  • plan done checks the wrong thread.
  • After exit, the next niuse launch resumes the old thread, not the one the user just worked in.

Scope

  • Let an embedder choose the new-session path, or receive on_session_start with the new path.
  • Update CompanionHooks::thread and keep thread.jsonl as the active thread (archive the old one through niuse semantics).
  • A PTY test must prove /new archives, clears context, and leaves product commands pointed at the new file.

Acceptance

  • /new creates a niuse-understood active thread.
  • /evidence after /new reads the new session.
  • /verify and plan commands append to the new session.
  • The old thread is archived under threads/.
  • A PTY regression covers archive and context isolation.

Notes

2026-10-22: fixed by niucode 323a158. TurnHooks::new_session_path archives thread.jsonl, returns the same active path, and on_session_start updates the hooks. /clear and /reset both use it. The PTY test starts a second thread, sees only SECOND_ANSWER in thread.jsonl, and finds FIRST_ANSWER in the archived file.

cards.title: TUI /reset session isolation
cards.body_html:
Problem

/new was proven to archive the old thread and reset thread.jsonl, but /reset shares the same new_session_path seam and had no PTY coverage. A regression there would leave plan/goal cleared while product commands still pointed at the old log.

Scope

  • Parameterize the PTY test for /new and /reset.
  • Both commands must archive the old thread, leave only the new answer in thread.jsonl, and keep the old answer only in the archive.
  • The hook pointer must be updated by on_session_start for both.

Acceptance

  • /new PTY isolation passes.
  • /reset PTY isolation passes.
  • Both archive the old log under threads/.
  • thread.jsonl contains only the second answer in both cases.
  • One script drives both modes; no copy-pasted harness.

Notes

/reset additionally clears plan/goal/history, but the session-path behavior is the risk this test covers. The parser and new-session seam remain unchanged.

cards.title: TUI /resume pointer PTY
cards.body_html:
Problem

/resume was wired to on_session_start, but only a unit test checked the notification. The real risk is a product command writing to the wrong thread after the switch.

Scope

  • PTY: run one turn, /new to archive it, run a second turn, /resume the archived file, then /verify p-1 true.
  • The verification must land in the resumed file, not the active thread.
  • Plan p-1 is created in the temp home before the TUI starts.

Acceptance

  • /resume prints resumed and switches the session.
  • /verify p-1 writes verification with step: p-1 to the resumed file.
  • The active thread.jsonl has no verification event.
  • The archived FIRST_ANSWER survives.
  • Runs under cargo test -p niuse --features tui.

Notes

Cross-restart active-thread semantics are still separate: exiting after /resume leaves thread.jsonl as the active file. This test proves the in-session pointer, which is what /evidence, /verify, and plan commands use.

cards.title: Active-thread decision after resume
cards.body_html:
Problem

/resume and /fork updated the live pointer but not the next launch's active thread. Leaving that ambiguous invited either a stale pointer file or silent archive rewriting.

Scope

  • ADR-0007 decides: thread.jsonl is the only active line across restarts.
  • /resume and /fork are session-scoped views, not promotions.
  • /new and /reset are the only cross-restart active-line changes.
  • Document the rule in architecture and status.

Acceptance

  • A pointer file is explicitly rejected.
  • Archive promotion is explicitly rejected.
  • In-session hooks still follow /resume (M5-006).
  • /new//reset archive and reset thread.jsonl.
  • Status and architecture say which command changes the next launch.

Notes

This closes the open product decision from M5-006 without new code. If real users need a chapter to become the main line, the explicit fallback is export or manual file movement.

cards.title: TUI /fork pointer PTY
cards.body_html:
Problem

/fork was wired to on_session_start, but the unit test only proved the notification helper. The real risk is a product command writing to the source thread after a fork.

Scope

  • PTY: run one turn, /fork, then /verify p-1 true.
  • The verification must land in the fork destination, not the source thread.
  • Plan p-1 is created in the temp home before the TUI starts.

Acceptance

  • /fork prints fork · and opens the destination.
  • /verify p-1 writes verification with step: p-1 to the fork file.
  • The source thread.jsonl has no verification event.
  • The fork contains FORK_SOURCE_ANSWER.
  • Runs under cargo test -p niuse --features tui.

Notes

ADR-0007 still applies: the fork is the live session for this run, not the next launch's thread.jsonl.

cards.title: TUI memory prompt PTY
cards.body_html:
Problem

The after-turn memory prompt was unit-tested through on_answer but never driven through the terminal. It uses blocking stdin while the TUI owns the terminal, so key mapping or read behavior could differ from the REPL.

Scope

  • Replay a turn containing a <<niuse:memory>> block.
  • Accept with 1; the candidate must appear in memory/.
  • Discard with 3; the candidate must not appear.
  • Assert the visible answer and the prompt question appear first.

Acceptance

  • VISIBLE_ANSWER renders.
  • The new memory prompt and options render.
  • 1 stores the candidate.
  • 3 does not store it.
  • The edit path is not automated (it would launch $EDITOR).

Notes

The prompt reads terminal input line-by-line; \r submits correctly in the PTY. The edit option remains covered only by unit tests because it opens an external editor.

cards.title: TUI records turn metrics
cards.body_html:
Problem

A real TUI turn on 2026-10-23 read a file and answered, but niuse dogfood recorded 0 turns. CompanionHooks did not implement on_turn_end, so TUI turns never reached metrics.jsonl; stats, report, and the dogfood gate could not see TUI work.

Scope

  • Implement on_turn_end: append tokens when usage is non-zero and turn ok.
  • Match the REPL's metric format.
  • Unit-test through Box<dyn TurnHooks> so the trait-object path is covered.
  • Re-run a real TUI task and wait for the metric before recording the day.

Acceptance

  • TUI on_turn_end writes tokens and turn.
  • The test calls through a trait object, not only the concrete hook.
  • A real TUI turn writes the metric before exit.
  • niuse stats --days 1 reports 1 turn.
  • niuse dogfood records 1 turn for 2026-10-23.

Notes

The first post-fix PTY run was killed before the post-turn hook ran; the metric appeared only after waiting for completion. The hook implementation is the product fix; the harness now waits for it.

cards.title: TUI brief/report/steps composition
cards.body_html:
Problem

/brief, /report, and /steps were tested individually or through their CLI commands, but not run back-to-back in one TUI session. That is the path a user actually takes when deciding what to do next.

Scope

  • Seed a plan step, goal, overdue loop, and a dogfood row in a temp home.
  • Run /brief, /report, and /steps in one PTY session.
  • Assert the brief header/loop, the report header/Dogfood line, and the plan step.

Acceptance

  • /brief prints niuse brief and the overdue loop id.
  • /report prints # niuse weekly report and Dogfood:.
  • /steps prints p-1 check brief.
  • All three share one home and one command hook.
  • Runs under cargo test -p niuse --features tui.

Notes

The test uses a replay provider with no turns, so only the product commands are exercised. The seed data intentionally has an overdue loop and one open step.

cards.title: Startup brief
cards.body_html:
Problem

The startup banner reports counts, but not what needs attention: an overdue promise with its due date, an unchecked bootstrap queue, or memory that has expired and should be pruned. The companion knows these facts and still waits to be asked.

Scope

  • Build a pure niuse-core brief from the existing stores: memory totals, stale and expired counts, open and overdue loops, the last journal day, and the unchecked inbox count.
  • Add niuse brief [--json], /brief in the REPL and TUI, and a compact actionable block after the interactive banner.
  • Keep it offline: no provider, no model call, no writes.
  • Add NIUSE_BRIEF=off for people who want the old quiet banner.

Acceptance

  • niuse brief --json reports counts, overdue loop ids/dates, and the last journal day.
  • The startup block lists at most three overdue loops and the review queue; it prints nothing when there is nothing actionable.
  • /brief works in the REPL and the TUI.
  • Unit tests cover empty, stale/expired, overdue, and inbox cases.
  • NIUSE_BRIEF=off suppresses only the automatic block.

Notes

Derived view only: no new store, no new event type, no second source of truth.

cards.title: Project registry
cards.body_html:
Problem

The companion can remember a preference but cannot answer "what was I doing last week, and in which repository?" niucode already stores per-project sessions under ~/.niucode/projects/*/project.toml; niuse neither reads nor surfaces them.

Scope

  • Read the niucode project registry read-only: recorded working directory, last session activity, and session count.
  • Add niuse projects [--limit N] [--json], sorted by most recent activity.
  • Show the current project and its most recent thread in niuse status.
  • Tolerate missing, corrupt, or moved project directories; never write there.
  • Keep the event log as the authority for a session; this is a directory view, not a second index.

Acceptance

  • A project appears once, with its recorded path and latest activity.
  • Unreadable entries are skipped with a warning; a missing cwd is flagged and hidden from the default view.
  • --json is stable and has no absolute paths beyond the recorded cwd.
  • Tests cover ordering, filtering, limits, corrupt entries, and an empty registry.
  • No files under ~/.niucode are created or modified.

Notes

This is the data source for a future "what changed while I was away" brief; do not add that behaviour here.

cards.title: Session digest into the journal
cards.body_html:
Problem

The journal is written by the model from in-band blocks during a turn. When a long thread ends, the decisions and turning points are still only in the transcript; the next session starts without them. Re-reading the thread is not a memory strategy.

Scope

  • Add an explicit niuse digest [--thread PATH] [--dry-run] that summarizes a finished thread into the journal, with source ids and no code dumps.
  • Use a separate, tool-free model call with a strict prompt; never write on a failed parse.
  • Keep the existing in-band journal as the default. The digest is opt-in until ten real digests are reviewed.
  • Exclude tool output and secrets; run the same scan as every journal write.

Acceptance

  • A scripted-provider test proves the summary is written once, uses only user/assistant text, and never writes tool output.
  • --dry-run prints the entry without writing.
  • A failed, empty, or malformed response writes nothing and says why.
  • Ten real digests are reviewed before the path becomes automatic.
  • The journal format and existing day-merging behaviour are unchanged.

Notes

2026-10-22: reviewed three real --dry-run outputs:

  • write session (1792683203856-421044-0): 4 bullets, task, decision, and due loop survived; no code dump.

  • MCP session (1792683062106-403780-0): 2 bullets, source id, no raw tool output. Quality caveat: it summarizes activity rather than a change; a short successful task has little to distill.

  • RSS disagreement session (1792683287429-436740-0): 5 bullets, captures the decision, three reasons, and the newly identified network-egress risk.

  • routine session (1792683461440-469411-0): 2 bullets, still activity-only after prompt tightening. The session also contained an unresolved due loop, so the gate correctly said YES; activity-only output remains a known limit.

  • trivial session (1792683490175-471215-0): the new pre-check said NO, so no digest call and no journal write.

  • old-loop routine (1792683461440-469411-0), after the gate revision: NO, because the only "unresolved" item was a pre-existing loop reminder.

  • RSS decision session, re-run: YES, 3 bullets (down from 5, more concise).

The gate now prints a one-line reason with every verdict. Real validation: RSS → YES · 助手明确反对...; trivial → NO · 用户仅要求回复数字391....

  • README Q&A (1792683015455-395814-0): NO with reason “只是读取文档并复述 已有命令，没有新决定或转折”. A correct no-change.

  • trivial 391 (1792683490175-471215-0): NO, no change. Counted as the sixth real review.

  • plan+verify (1792683740897-529410-0): YES with reason. One bullet captured the recommendation and the open rename/delete decision. The [verification] line was available but the digest chose not to include it; a weak file check is not the decision.

  • plan check failed then fixed (1792683789646-539240-0): after the gate rule change, YES with reason. Two bullets: the initial failure and the repaired pass. Before the change this session was a false NO.

  • unresolved failure (1792683839496-548634-0): YES because the failed p-1 check created an open decision. One bullet says the check failed and the choice is README vs step, with no invented repair.

  • memory Q&A (1792683247889-429410-0): initially YES because the answer restated m-3d0b; after the restatement gate rule, NO with reason “仅复述 已注入的长期记忆内容”.

That is 10/10 real reviews. Decision: keep the digest opt-in. Automatic journal writes would add a model call and noise to every thread; the gate is still model-dependent, and no real user asked for automatic. The card is done for the opt-in feature, not for automatic writes. Activity-only digests are a known limitation, not a reason to auto-write.

The source thread is named in the command output and recorded in the digest metric; the journal itself stays plain bullets. Do not summarize every turn: the journal records change, not activity.

cards.title: Unified recall across stores
cards.body_html:
Problem

Full injection is capped at about 2k tokens; entries outside the cap or past expiry are invisible to the model even though they are still in the stores. A human can search memory one command at a time, but not memory, journal, promises, and goals together, and the model has no honest way to ask for an old entry.

Scope

  • One bounded, read-only search over memory (including expired), journal bullets, loops, and goals.
  • niuse recall <query> [--limit N] [--json], /recall in the REPL and TUI.
  • Rank with the existing lexical score, label freshness, and cap the result.
  • Tell the model in the protocol that it may ask the user to run /recall <关键词> when it suspects a missing old memory; it must not guess.

Acceptance

  • A query returns hits from all four stores with ids, dates, and detail.
  • Expired memory is included and labelled.
  • The result is capped and JSON is available for scripts.
  • Offline tests cover hit, miss, empty store, and the limit.
  • The model is told to request /recall instead of inventing a memory.

Notes

This is the human-facing half. The model still cannot invoke recall by itself; that needs a generic tool seam in niucode and is tracked as M6-005.

cards.title: Agent-invoked memory recall
cards.body_html:
Problem

M6-004 gives the human /recall, and the prompt tells the model to ask for it. That still costs a round trip and depends on the user being present. A stronger companion can retrieve a missing old judgement inside the turn and cite it.

Scope

  • Add a generic, read-only tool seam in niucode that an embedder can register without forking the loop or adding personal schema to niucode-core.
  • Register a bounded memory_search tool from niuse over the same store as /recall; results carry ids, dates, and freshness.
  • Keep full injection as the default; recall is additive and cannot write, delete, or confirm memory.
  • Budget the result and never dump the whole store into context.

Acceptance

  • A turn retrieves a matching entry and receives its id and freshness in the tool result.
  • The tool cannot write, delete, or confirm memory.
  • The result is capped by the query limit and reuses unified recall.
  • Offline tests cover a hit, an empty query, and a full scripted turn.
  • The seam is generic and has a niucode contract test (M5-010).

Notes

The tool is registered in the REPL, exec, and TUI paths through AgentConfig.extra_tools; it is read-only and therefore needs no approval. Memory is already secret-scanned at the write, so recall introduces no new write surface. niucode caps tool output and compacts the conversation; the query limit keeps the result small. The memory semantics stay in niuse.

cards.title: Digest NONE is a no-change
cards.body_html:
Problem

The digest prompt tells the model to output NONE when nothing durable happened, but the command treated that as an error ("no journal entries"). A healthy no-change day looked like a failure, and an explicit signal was indistinguishable from malformed chatter.

Scope

  • NONE (case-insensitive, trimmed) exits 0, prints no-change, writes nothing, and records no digest metric.
  • Empty or prose-only output remains an error.
  • Dry-run reports the same no-change.
  • Tests cover both branches and the metric.

Acceptance

  • NONE is a success with no journal write.
  • No digest metric is recorded for NONE.
  • Prose without bullets still fails.
  • Dry-run says there is nothing to write.
  • Secret refusal and five-bullet cap are unchanged.

Notes

This addresses the activity-only caveat from M6-003: a short successful task can legitimately have nothing to distill. It does not make the digest automatic.

cards.title: Digest no-change pre-check
cards.body_html:
Problem

Tightening the digest prompt did not stop activity summaries: a routine create-and-confirm task still produced two bullets. The model was using the digest call to summarize what happened because that is what the call asks for.

Scope

  • One cheap YES/NO gate before the digest call.
  • NO: exit 0, no journal, no metric, same output as explicit NONE.
  • YES: run the existing digest.
  • Anything else: error without writing.
  • Tests for NO, YES, malformed gate, and the existing branches.

Acceptance

  • A trivial session returns NO and writes nothing.
  • A routine session with an unresolved due loop returns YES; that is a real unresolved issue, not activity.
  • Gate NO records no digest metric.
  • Gate YES still caps at five bullets and scans secrets.
  • Malformed gate output fails closed.

Notes

The gate costs one extra small model call per digest. It is opt-in and far cheaper than writing an activity journal. The prompt-tightening change stays; the gate is the reliable layer.

cards.title: Digest gate ignores old-loop reminders
cards.body_html:
Problem

The YES/NO gate counted a reminder of an old due loop as a "new unresolved problem", so a routine session still passed and produced activity bullets.

Scope

  • Gate prompt distinguishes new/advanced issues from reminders of pre-existing items; an old loop reminder alone is NO.
  • Real validation both ways: old-loop routine → NO; RSS disagreement → YES.
  • No change to the digest call or write path.

Acceptance

  • Routine session with only an old-loop reminder returns NO.
  • RSS decision session still returns YES and produces bullets.
  • The digest call count drops for old-reminder sessions.
  • Gate NO writes nothing and records no metric.
  • Existing gate and NONE tests pass.

Notes

Prompt-only classification remains model-dependent. The real two-way check is the evidence; a future hardening could return a one-line reason with the gate verdict for audit.

cards.title: Digest gate verdict and reason
cards.body_html:
Problem

The YES/NO gate was auditable only by its verdict. A wrong YES or NO could not be explained without another model call.

Scope

  • Gate returns one line: YES: reason or NO: reason.
  • Parse verdict case-insensitively; a bare YES/NO is still accepted with a placeholder reason; anything else fails closed.
  • Print the reason on YES and on NO (dry-run and real).
  • Increase the gate token cap to fit one sentence.
  • Parse tests for YES, NO, bare verdict, and malformed output.

Acceptance

  • YES verdicts print their reason before the digest.
  • NO verdicts include the reason in the no-change message.
  • Bare legacy verdicts still work.
  • Malformed verdicts write nothing.
  • Real validation: RSS → YES with a reason; trivial → NO with a reason.

Notes

Reasons are model prose and can be wrong; the verdict and its reason are shown together so the human can judge. Reasons are not stored in the journal or metrics.

cards.title: Digest includes verification evidence
cards.body_html:
Problem

The digest transcript was user/assistant prose only. A session that ended with a recorded verification looked like a conversation with no evidence, so the digest could not say whether a step passed or failed.

Scope

  • Include verification events as compact lines: [verification] p-1 ok cargo test / FAILED.
  • Keep the command, verdict, and optional step; never include tool output.
  • Count these lines against the same recent-item and character budgets.
  • Test the transcript shape.

Acceptance

  • A recorded verification appears in the transcript with step and verdict.
  • Failed verifications say FAILED.
  • Tool output is still excluded.
  • The recent-item limit applies to messages and verifications together.
  • Existing digest, gate, NONE, and secret tests pass.

Notes

2026-10-22 real plan+verify run: the [verification] p-1 ok grep ... line reached the transcript, but the digest kept the decision and open question instead. That is acceptable: a weak file existence check is not the change. Verification evidence is human-run and bounded at write time; including it is not a tool-output leak.

cards.title: Digest captures failed-then-fixed verification
cards.body_html:
Problem

A plan step failed its check, the file was repaired, and the re-check passed. The gate still said NO: "read the file and report, then verification failed and passed, no new decision". That is exactly the experience the journal should keep.

Scope

  • Gate: a failed verification followed by a passing one is a turning point.
  • Digest prompt: record the failure cause and repair, not only the final pass.
  • No new events or hidden tool output; verification lines already carry the verdict and command.

Acceptance

  • The same session now returns YES with that reason.
  • Digest produces a bullet for the initial failure.
  • Digest produces a bullet for the repair/final pass.
  • The final pass is not the only record.
  • Existing NO cases (old loop, Q&A, trivial) still pass.

Notes

This does not make every failed check a journal entry: the failure must be repaired and followed by a pass inside the session. Unresolved failures remain covered by the "new unresolved issue" rule.

cards.title: Digest keeps unresolved failures open
cards.body_html:
Problem

The positive failed-then-fixed case is recorded, but the negative case matters more: an unresolved failed check must never be summarized as success.

Scope

  • Real plan step, real model turn, one failed verification, no repair.
  • Gate should say YES (new unresolved issue), digest should say failed and name the open choice, never "passed".
  • No code change unless the output lies.

Acceptance

  • Gate reason says the check failed and an open decision exists.
  • Digest bullet says 验证失败, not passed.
  • The open choice (fix README vs adjust the step) is preserved.
  • No repair is invented.
  • M6-003 reaches 9/10 real reviews.

Notes

This is the guardrail for M6-011: recording a repair must not train the digest to assume every failure gets fixed. The two cases are now both evidenced.

cards.title: Gate ignores restated memory
cards.body_html:
Problem

The tenth real digest was a memory Q&A: the assistant restated m-3d0b. The gate said YES because the content was "new in the conversation", even though it existed in the store before the session. The digest then repeated a preference, which the digest prompt explicitly forbids.

Scope

  • Gate rule: restating injected memory is not new information; only a memory being changed, challenged, or used for a new decision counts.
  • Re-run the same real session; expect NO with that reason.
  • No new code beyond the gate prompt.

Acceptance

  • Memory Q&A returns NO with a restatement reason.
  • The digest call is skipped; no journal, no metric.
  • A real decision session still returns YES (RSS).
  • Old-loop, trivial, Q&A, and failed/repair cases unchanged.
  • M6-003 reaches 10/10 real reviews.

Notes

This is the final gate hardening for the ten-review sample. It stays model-dependent; the reason line makes a wrong YES auditable.

cards.title: Persistent human-owned goals
cards.body_html:
Problem

loops.md holds the companion's promises, not the human's outcomes. niucode's /goal is a session condition and disappears when a new thread starts. A long-horizon companion needs a small, human-owned statement of what the work is for, injected into every session.

Scope

  • ~/.niuse/goals.md with g- ids, one sentence, creation date, open/done.
  • niuse goals list|add|done and /goals in the REPL and TUI.
  • Inject open goals after user and before memory, budget 300 tokens.
  • Enforce at most seven open goals and refuse secrets at the write.
  • The model reads goals but never writes them.

Acceptance

  • A goal survives a new process and is injected into the prompt.
  • goals add|done and /goals round-trip in the REPL and TUI.
  • More than seven open goals is refused.
  • Secret-looking goals are refused and nothing is written.
  • brief and status report open goals.
  • ADR-0006 records the ownership and store decision.

Notes

No due dates, priorities, or progress percentages. Those belong in loops.md or a human project plan; this store is a compass, not a tracker.

cards.title: Read-only plan mode in the REPL
cards.body_html:
Problem

niucode's TUI has /plan, but the default REPL does not. Before a multi-step change, the companion should be able to investigate and propose a plan without being able to write files or run mutating commands. The TUI path should not be required for a safe planning pass.

Scope

  • --plan starts a session in plan mode; /plan [on|off] toggles it.
  • Plan mode sets AgentConfig.plan_mode and narrows allowed_tools to read, grep, and glob.
  • Protocol writes (memory, loop, journal) are ignored while planning.
  • The banner shows · plan so the restricted state is visible.
  • exec --plan gets the same treatment.

Acceptance

  • /plan on narrows the tool allowlist and turns on the plan prompt.
  • /plan off restores the normal tool surface.
  • Protocol blocks are not written during a plan turn.
  • --plan starts the REPL and exec in plan mode.
  • The TUI receives TuiOptions.plan from the same flag.

Notes

The prompt instruction comes from niucode; niuse only selects the mode and the allowlist. No new store and no second approval path.

cards.title: Thread evidence report
cards.body_html:
Problem

After a long execute phase, the final answer is a claim. The thread already contains what actually ran: which tools were called, which files were touched, which checks ran, what failed, and which approvals were denied. That evidence was visible only by scrolling the transcript.

Scope

  • Read-only Evidence derived from assistant_message.tool_calls and tool_result events.
  • List write/edit paths, test-like bash checks with pass/fail, total failures, and denied approvals.
  • niuse evidence [--thread PATH] [--json], /evidence in the REPL and TUI.
  • No new store and no new event type.

Acceptance

  • A thread with a write and cargo test reports one file and one passing check.
  • A failed tool and a denied approval are counted separately.
  • Empty threads say there is no evidence instead of implying success.
  • JSON is stable for scripts.
  • The report is available in the REPL and TUI.

Notes

This separates "ran and succeeded" from "the answer said so". It does not prove the task is correct; that still needs a real verification command chosen for the task. Test-like commands are a heuristic over bash text.

cards.title: Recorded verification command
cards.body_html:
Problem

/evidence could show checks that happened to run during an agent turn, but a human still had to scroll the transcript to prove a task after execution. There was no first-class way to say "this is the command that decides", run it, and keep the result in the thread.

Scope

  • verification event in niucode: command, ok, bounded output tail.
  • niuse verify -- <command> runs it, prints the tail, appends the event, and exits with the command's status.
  • /verify <command> in the REPL does the same without leaving the session.
  • /evidence lists recorded verifications separately from agent-run checks.
  • The event is ignored by model-context projection; it is evidence, not conversation.

Acceptance

  • A passing command appends ok: true and exits 0.
  • A failing command appends ok: false and exits non-zero.
  • JSON output includes command, code, output tail, and thread path.
  • Output is capped at 4k characters on a char boundary.
  • /evidence reports recorded verifications.
  • The event round-trips through the session log.

Notes

The human chooses the command; this does not infer what "verified" means for a task and does not run through the agent's approval path. That is deliberate: it is a human assertion with a reproducible command attached.

cards.title: Verification-gated plan ledger
cards.body_html:
Problem

The plan existed only in the transcript. A step could be called done with no durable evidence, and verification events were not tied to the step they proved.

Scope

  • plan.md: human-owned steps with p-N labels and a done bit.
  • niuse plan list|add|done, capped open steps, secret-scanned add.
  • niuse verify --step p-N tags the verification event.
  • plan done p-N refuses unless the current thread has a passing verification for that step.
  • niuse evidence renders plan steps with verified / no recorded verification.

Acceptance

  • Steps get stable p-N labels and survive reload.
  • plan done is refused without a passing step-tagged verification.
  • A passing verification closes the step.
  • Evidence JSON carries both plan state and the verification's step.
  • The CLI lifecycle test covers add → refused → verify → done.
  • Existing verification events without a step still parse.

Notes

2026-10-22 real run: with p-1 injected (M7-006), the model read the file, refused to mark the step done because it had no verification evidence, and asked which direction to take. The human ran verify --step p-1 -- grep ..., the check passed, and plan done 1 closed the step. This is the gate working against a real provider, not a scripted turn.

cards.title: Inject the open plan into the prompt
cards.body_html:
Problem

plan.md was a human ledger. The agent never saw the steps, so it could not work toward them or warn that a step had no verification.

Scope

  • compose_with_plan: goals, then open plan steps, then memory.
  • Only open steps, at most six, within a 300-token budget.
  • State the completion rule: verify with niuse verify --step p-N before claiming a step is done.
  • Pass the plan through the REPL, TUI, /prompt, and eval composition.

Acceptance

  • Open steps appear under 当前计划 with their p-N labels.
  • Done steps are omitted.
  • An all-done plan adds no section.
  • The section states the verification command.
  • The plan sits between goals and memory.
  • The offline eval covers the injection.

Notes

The plan is still human-owned; the model cannot add or close steps. That mutation stays behind niuse plan, so the verification gate cannot be self-approved.

cards.title: Delegation evidence
cards.body_html:
Problem

niucode's subagent tool already delegates read-only work, but the parent thread recorded spawn/result events that neither the human nor niuse evidence surfaced. Delegated work was invisible unless the transcript was scrolled.

Scope

  • Read subagent_spawn / subagent_result from the thread.
  • Report profile, task, session, turns, ok, and summary.
  • A spawn without a result reports ?, never success.
  • niuse evidence --json includes the delegation array.
  • Pin subagent availability in the niucode contract test.

Acceptance

  • Completed explore runs show ✓ and their summary.
  • An unfinished spawn shows ? and no success claim.
  • The task, profile, session, and turn count are visible.
  • JSON carries the same data.
  • The contract test fails if the subagent tool disappears.

Notes

This is read-only delegation through niucode's tool; niuse does not add a second orchestrator. Worker writes remain a niucode concern with its own write lock.

cards.title: TUI plan and verify surface
cards.body_html:
Problem

The REPL and CLI had /verify and niuse plan, but inside the TUI the plan ledger was invisible and verification could not be tagged to a step without leaving the session.

Scope

  • /steps lists open steps with verification state.
  • /steps add <text> creates a step.
  • /steps done <N> closes it through the same verification gate as the CLI.
  • /verify [p-N] <command> runs and records a check, tagging the step.
  • Commands appear in help and completion.

Acceptance

  • /steps add returns a p-N label.
  • /steps shows no recorded verification until a check passes.
  • /steps done refuses without a passing tagged verification.
  • /verify p-1 true passes and /steps done 1 closes the step.
  • The commands are listed for help/completion.
  • They share the CLI gate instead of a second implementation.

Notes

/plan remains niucode's read-only plan-mode toggle; /steps is the niuse ledger. Keeping them separate avoids overloading one command with two modes.

cards.title: TUI plan/verify PTY regression
cards.body_html:
Problem

/steps and step-tagged /verify were covered only at the hook level. A real terminal also has completion, redraw, and command routing, and /evidence forgot to attach the plan store, so the PTY test exposed a gap.

Scope

  • PTY test types the full flow: add → refused done → verify → done → evidence.
  • Assert the plan file, the thread verification, and the visible states.
  • Fix TUI /evidence to attach store.plan() like the CLI command.

Acceptance

  • /steps add shows added p-1.
  • /steps shows no recorded verification.
  • /steps done is refused with no passing verification.
  • /verify p-1 true passes and /steps done 1 closes.
  • /steps then says no open steps.
  • /evidence shows the verified plan step.
  • plan.md has [x] p-1; the thread has the tagged verification.

Notes

The regression found a real bug: the TUI evidence report omitted plan steps. The test is the reason the fix exists, not a ceremonial replay.

cards.title: Mount MCP in the REPL and exec
cards.body_html:
Problem

niucode mounted read-only MCP servers in exec and the TUI, but niuse's own REPL and exec build AgentConfig directly. Users could use MCP tools in niuse tui but not in the default front end.

Scope

  • Mount through niucode-mcp::McpHost from NIUSE_MCP_CONFIG or ~/.niucode/mcp.toml.
  • Attach the host to every turn's AgentConfig, not just the TUI's.
  • Shut the host down at REPL/exec exit.
  • A broken manifest warns and disables MCP for that run; it does not fail the session.

Acceptance

  • The REPL and exec set AgentConfig.mcp_host.
  • NIUSE_MCP_CONFIG overrides the default path.
  • Host shutdown runs on normal exit.
  • An offline test mounts the fixture server from a manifest and calls a namespaced tool.
  • ./scripts/check.sh is green.

Notes

The mount is read-only by construction; secrets never enter the child environment unless the manifest names them.

cards.title: Read-only notes MCP pack
cards.body_html:
Problem

MCP v1 was proven against a synthetic fixture, not a real personal source. The connected-agent claim needs one pack that a person can point at real data and one test that proves the boundary holds.

Scope

  • packs/notes/server.py: a standard-library stdio MCP server over NOTES_DIR.
  • Read-only tools: search_notes, read_note, list_notes.
  • Resolve paths before confinement; reject .. and escaping symlinks.
  • Cap reads and search hits; skip hidden files.
  • Manifest example and setup notes in packs/notes/README.md.
  • End-to-end test through McpHost.

Acceptance

  • Search returns file:line hits from real Markdown/text notes.
  • read_note returns bounded UTF-8 content.
  • ../escape.md is a tool error, not a file read.
  • The server has no write tool and no network dependency.
  • McpHost mounts it and the namespaced tools dispatch.
  • A setup example exists for ~/.niucode/mcp.toml.

Notes

This is the first real pack, not a general file manager. A mutating pack waits for the approval design in ADR-0033's follow-up.

cards.title: Read-only calendar MCP pack
cards.body_html:
Problem

The connected agent proved one personal source (notes). A second, different shape of data is needed to show the MCP seam generalizes without a new kernel feature.

Scope

  • packs/calendar/server.py: standard-library stdio MCP server over one ICS.
  • list_events(days) and search_events(query, limit).
  • Unfold ICS lines, unescape text, parse date and time, sort, cap.
  • CALENDAR_ICS required; CALENDAR_TODAY for deterministic tests.
  • End-to-end test through McpHost.

Acceptance

  • A timed event and an all-day event are listed.
  • An event outside the window is not listed.
  • Search matches description text and returns no matches cleanly.
  • The server has no write tool and no network dependency.
  • The pack mounts through the same read-only MCP host as notes.
  • A manifest example is documented.

Notes

Single-file, read-only, no timezone conversion. Calendar subscriptions, timezones, and writes need separate designs; writes are blocked on ADR-0034.

cards.title: MCP onboarding with bundled packs
cards.body_html:
Problem

The packs existed, but onboarding meant reading source, finding absolute paths, and hand-writing TOML. A personal agent that needs a manifest tutorial is not ready for personal use.

Scope

  • niuse mcp init --notes DIR --calendar FILE.
  • Write bundled server scripts to ~/.niuse/packs/ (or --packs).
  • Write ~/.niucode/mcp.toml (or --config) with read-only entries.
  • Resolve an absolute python3 path, because the child environment is scrubbed.
  • Refuse to overwrite an existing manifest without --force; no silent merge.
  • Private dirs/files; scripts executable.
  • End-to-end test mounts the generated manifest and calls both packs.

Acceptance

  • One command writes scripts and a manifest.
  • The generated manifest validates and mounts.
  • Notes search and calendar search both work through it.
  • An existing manifest is refused without --force.
  • Python is stored as an absolute path.
  • --config / --packs make the test hermetic.

Notes

No merge: replacing a trust file silently would be worse than asking for --force. Mutating servers remain out of scope; the generated manifest has only read_only = true.

cards.title: Safe MCP manifest merge
cards.body_html:
Problem

mcp init refused any existing trust file unless --force, which replaced the whole file. Adding the calendar pack after notes would have deleted a user's other servers and comments.

Scope

  • Parse the existing manifest; if it is invalid, stop before writing.
  • Merge by server name: add missing requested servers, keep existing ones.
  • Preserve all existing text, including comments and formatting.
  • --force still means replace.
  • Report added / kept / unchanged.

Acceptance

  • Notes-only manifest + calendar init produces both servers.
  • The original text and a custom comment survive the merge.
  • Re-running with both present is a no-op.
  • Invalid TOML fails and leaves the file byte-identical.
  • --force still replaces the file.
  • The generated merged manifest still mounts.

Notes

Name collision is the merge key; a user server named notes is kept, not overwritten. There is no reordering or comment-aware TOML rewrite.

cards.title: TUI MCP mount PTY regression
cards.body_html:
Problem

The TUI MCP path was wired but only the exec path had an end-to-end test. A regression in niuse's TuiOptions or niucode's default manifest path would only show up in manual use.

Scope

  • PTY test with NIUCODE_HOME pointing at a temp manifest.
  • Replay provider calls mcp__notes__search_notes.
  • Assert the startup mcp: notes line, the visible answer, and a successful tool result containing the note path in the append-only thread.
  • No API key or network; reuses the notes pack and Python PTY harness.

Acceptance

  • TUI mounts the notes server from $NIUCODE_HOME/mcp.toml.
  • Replay calls the namespaced MCP tool.
  • The thread records a successful tool_result with note.md.
  • The startup mount line is visible.
  • Runs under cargo test -p niuse --features tui and check.sh.

Notes

This is a protocol regression, not a renderer certification. It closes the M8-001 follow-up note.

cards.title: Mount write-enabled MCP in niuse
cards.body_html:
Problem

niucode now implements the accepted ADR-0034 write path (write_tools, --allow-mcp-write, per-call approval, write lock), but niuse does not expose the flag or ship a write-enabled pack. The product still mounts read-only servers only.

Scope

  • Add --allow-mcp-write to niuse exec and niuse tui, passed to niucode-mcp mount.
  • Refuse it with --json, --approval never, or a non-interactive run.
  • Ship at least one write pack with an explicit write_tools allowlist.
  • The TUI approval prompt shows the namespaced tool and bounded arguments.
  • Integration test: deny writes nothing; allow writes once.

Acceptance

  • niuse exposes the flag and forwards it without changing read-only defaults.
  • --never and a non-terminal mount read-only servers only.
  • A write pack lists every mutating tool; unlisted tools stay read-only.
  • TUI approval shows tool + args; denial leaves the store unchanged.
  • Offline test covers mount refusal and an approved write.

Notes

niucode ab50b75 is the implementation. This card is the niuse surface, not a second design; ADR-0034 remains the source of truth.

2026-10-23: the flag and mount gating are in (app.allow_mcp_write, driver mount_mcp_from_with, unit test). TUI forwards it to niucode. The notes pack now has opt-in create_note, and mcp_notes_write.rs proves denial writes nothing and approval writes once. 2026-10-23: tui_mcp_write.rs covers both outcomes. The PTY waits for the namespaced tool and the Arguments: preview, sends n or y, and checks the note file. Deny writes nothing; allow writes once. The card is done.

cards.title: Evidence shows MCP mounts
cards.body_html:
Problem

ADR-0034 added mcp_mount events, but niuse evidence ignored them. A user could see approvals and tool calls without seeing which servers were mounted, which tools could write, or the config hash.

Scope

  • Parse mcp_mount into Evidence.mounts.
  • Render server · read-only or server · writes: … · hash.
  • Include mounts in the evidence header and in is_empty.
  • Assert the TUI /evidence path after a real mutating mount.

Acceptance

  • A mount-only thread is not reported empty.
  • The header counts mcp mounts.
  • The section shows server, write allowlist, and 16-hex hash.
  • The TUI PTY sees writes: and mcp mount(s) after /evidence.
  • Read-only mounts render as read-only.

Notes

This is presentation only; the event log remains the source. The hash is the same value niucode writes at mount, not a recomputation in niuse.

cards.title: Offline personal-agent eval
cards.body_html:
Problem

The personal agent changes through prompts, stores, tools, and MCP packs, but there was no named offline suite that says which capability broke. Unit tests cover modules; they do not cover the prompt → turn → answer chain as one case.

Scope

  • Named cases for memory injection, goal lifecycle, and the startup brief.
  • A real MCP pack case in the same runner.
  • A behavioural memory-on/off A/B, not just a string comparison.
  • ./scripts/eval.sh as the single command.
  • Document what the suite does and does not prove.

Acceptance

  • Memory-on and memory-off produce different answers, and only the on case cites the remembered text.
  • Open goals are injected; closed goals are not.
  • The brief reports overdue promises, stale memory, and the inbox.
  • The notes MCP pack is part of the runner.
  • ./scripts/eval.sh passes offline.
  • Recall through memory_search (fresh and expired) is covered.
  • MCP timeout and read-only refusal are covered by the runner.
  • A dogfood trend gate blocks a release on a real regression.

Notes

Cases use a scripted provider, so this is a plumbing and prompt regression suite. The MCP client/agent cases come from the sibling niucode workspace and are skipped if it is absent. Real usefulness still needs dogfood.

cards.title: Prompt-size regression budget
cards.body_html:
Problem

Every turn pays for the injected prompt. Memory, goals, plans, loops, and journal each have a budget, but no test proved the composed prompt stayed bounded as a store filled up. A truncation regression would quietly raise cost on every turn and could break the stable cache prefix.

Scope

  • A fat-store fixture: 200 memories, 7 goals, 6 plan steps, 20 promises, 10 journal days, identity, and user.
  • Assert total composed prompt ≤ 4,200 tokens and each section within its budget plus a small instruction allowance.
  • Plan flood: 50 steps inject six and say the rest are omitted.
  • Memory flood: 500 entries are dropped rather than appended.
  • Run through ./scripts/eval.sh.

Acceptance

  • Fat prompt is under 4,200 estimated tokens.
  • Each injected section is within its budget plus slack.
  • A 50-step plan injects six steps and reports the omission.
  • 500 memories produce dropped entries, not a longer prompt.
  • Composition.tokens matches the shared estimator.
  • The eval runner includes the case.

Notes

This is a token-count regression, not a provider bill. Prices and cache hits still need real usage; scripts/dogfood-trend.sh watches tokens per turn.

cards.title: Cost signals in stats
cards.body_html:
Problem

stats reported raw input/output/cached totals, but not the two numbers that explain a bill: how much of the input was cached, and how many tokens each turn cost. A regression in either was invisible unless a human did the division.

Scope

  • cache_hit_percent: cached / input, clamped to 100, null without input.
  • tokens_per_turn: (input + output) / turns, null without turns.
  • JSON fields plus two text lines.
  • Unit tests for the arithmetic and a CLI test for the JSON shape.

Acceptance

  • 1,000 input + 500 cached reports 50% cache hit.
  • 1,000 input + 200 output + 1 turn reports 1,200 tokens/turn.
  • No input or no turns reports null, not zero.
  • Cached > input is clamped to 100.
  • Text output labels both numbers.
  • The CLI test pins the JSON keys.

Notes

No price is guessed. The numbers are provider-agnostic; a future price table can multiply them without changing this schema.

cards.title: Combined personal workflow eval
cards.body_html:
Problem

The eval suite tested each piece: recall, goals, plan injection, MCP packs, verification. Nothing proved they compose into one personal workflow.

Scope

  • One agent turn with notes and calendar mounted together.
  • A real plan step created through the store.
  • The model calls both namespaced MCP tools.
  • A step-tagged verification is appended, the step closes, and niuse evidence --json shows both.
  • No API key, network, or real personal data.

Acceptance

  • Both packs mount into one host.
  • Calendar search returns the standup.
  • Notes search returns standup.md.
  • The plan step closes only after the tagged verification.
  • Evidence JSON reports plan done, verification step, and ≥2 tools.
  • The eval runner includes the case.

Notes

This is the cross-layer proof, not a model-quality claim. The provider is scripted; the value is that the harness, two adapters, the plan store, and the event log agree on one scenario.

cards.title: Multi-turn plan execution eval
cards.body_html:
Problem

The combined workflow proved a single turn. A plan that spans turns can fail differently: a completed step lingers in the prompt, or the next step runs without the previous one being verified.

Scope

  • Two real plan steps and two MCP packs.
  • Turn one calls notes, the test verifies and closes p-1.
  • Recompose: p-1 must disappear, p-2 must remain.
  • Turn two calls calendar, the test verifies and closes p-2.
  • Recompose: no 当前计划 section remains.
  • Evidence reports two done steps and two step-tagged verifications.

Acceptance

  • Both steps are present before turn one.
  • After p-1 closes, only p-2 is in the next prompt.
  • After p-2 closes, no plan section is injected.
  • Both tool results are in the thread.
  • Evidence shows both steps done and both verifications tagged.
  • The eval runner includes the case.

Notes

The human closes steps; the model cannot self-approve. This case checks the prompt transition between turns, which a single-turn test cannot see.

cards.title: Verification failure recovery
cards.body_html:
Problem

A step with a failed verification was rendered as no recorded verification, which looks like nothing ran. The step stayed open, but the UI hid the failure and invited the model to retry blindly.

Scope

  • Evidence::step_state: verified / verification failed / no recorded verification.
  • evidence and TUI /steps use the same state.
  • A failed check keeps the step in the next prompt and refuses plan done.
  • A later pass closes it; both the failed and passing checks stay in history.

Acceptance

  • A failed-only step says verification failed, not "none".
  • The step remains in the prompt after the failure.
  • plan done is refused until a pass exists.
  • A later passing check closes the step and removes the plan section.
  • Evidence JSON keeps both checks in order.
  • TUI /steps shows the failed state.

Notes

Failure is history, not an alarm: the passing check makes the step verified while the failed attempt remains visible. No automatic retry is introduced.

cards.title: Stable prompt prefix and protocol heading
cards.body_html:
Problem

Cache-hit rate depends on the bytes before ## 今天 staying identical when only the date, loops, or journal change. Nothing pinned that invariant, and the protocol section repeated its own ## 记忆协议 heading because the renderer already adds the title.

Scope

  • Test: volatile date/loops/journal do not change the stable prefix.
  • Test: memory changes do change it on purpose.
  • Test: goals and plan live inside the prefix.
  • Remove the duplicate protocol heading; assert it appears once.

Acceptance

  • Changing day, promise, and journal leaves the prefix byte-identical.
  • The full prompts still differ.
  • 记忆协议 appears before 今天, loops, and journal.
  • 记忆协议 appears once.
  • A memory change invalidates the prefix.
  • The plan and goal are in the prefix.

Notes

This is a structural cost regression, not a provider cache measurement. It protects the boundary the provider needs; real hit rates still come from stats.

cards.title: Documentation link check
cards.body_html:
Problem

Docs and cards link to ADRs, plans, and each other. A rename can leave a dead relative link that no test notices; two M4-002 links were already broken.

Scope

  • Scan README.md, AGENTS.md, and docs/**/*.md.
  • Check relative links, skipping http, anchors, mailto, and paths outside the repo; ignore fenced code blocks.
  • Fail on missing targets; run in check.sh.
  • Deterministic self-test with a valid and a missing link.

Acceptance

  • The two M4-002 links are fixed.
  • A valid relative link passes.
  • A missing relative link fails with its source.
  • Fenced code examples are ignored.
  • check.sh runs the live check and self-test.
  • External links and anchors are skipped.

Notes

This checks existence, not anchors. A heading rename inside a valid file is not detected; that would need a Markdown parser.

cards.title: Board consistency check
cards.body_html:
Problem

The dashboard validates card references but not state contradictions. The audit found M3 marked done while its distribution card was backlog, and M4 planned while its card was doing.

Scope

  • Parse milestone statuses and card frontmatter.
  • Reject:
    • a done milestone with a non-done card;
    • a doing card in a planned milestone;
    • done without completed;
    • blocked without blocked_reason;
    • unknown milestones or statuses.
  • Fix the two stale states: M3 is planned again; M4-001 is blocked on M5-002.
  • Allow multiple active milestones after M2 and M5 gates legitimately overlap.
  • Run live plus a deterministic self-test in check.sh.

Acceptance

  • M3 no longer claims done while packaging is backlog.
  • M4-001 is blocked with a concrete reason, not doing in a planned phase.
  • Open card in a done milestone fails.
  • Doing card in a planned milestone fails.
  • Blocked without reason fails.
  • The live board passes.

Notes

Multiple active milestones are allowed: M2 dogfood and M5 TUI dogfood run in parallel. The earlier one-active rule was too strict. This checks state, not judgement; a milestone can still be marked done too early with all cards done.

cards.title: README command contract
cards.body_html:
Problem

README command examples can drift from clap, and the REPL command list can name a command that no longer exists. The docs test found /steps documented for the REPL but missing from SLASH_COMMANDS.

Scope

  • Parse fenced niuse <subcommand> examples; assert clap knows each one.
  • Parse the README's "Inside the REPL" list; assert every base command is in SLASH_COMMANDS.
  • Skip prose lines, comments, flags, and feature-gated tui.
  • Add /steps (list/add/done) to the REPL, sharing the CLI plan gate.

Acceptance

  • Every README CLI example names a real subcommand.
  • Every README REPL command is registered.
  • /steps works in the REPL, not only the TUI.
  • The tests fail on an unknown command.
  • check.sh runs them with the normal test suite.

Notes

This is a name-level contract, not an argument-level one. Flags can still drift; a future test could compare --help text.

cards.title: README flag contract
cards.body_html:
Problem

The name-level README test would pass even if a documented flag no longer exists. Synopsis lines such as loops list|add|done ... --overdue also need nested-subcommand awareness.

Scope

  • Parse fenced examples starting with niuse <subcommand>.
  • Collect long flags from the command, its immediate subcommands, and root globals.
  • Skip tui, flags-first lines, comments, and prose-only lines.
  • Assert every documented --flag exists.

Acceptance

  • A valid flag on a nested command passes (--overdue).
  • An unknown flag fails with the command and valid set.
  • Root globals are accepted.
  • Name-level and REPL contracts still pass.
  • The check runs in the normal test suite.

Notes

This is still a smoke contract: flags from sibling subcommands are accepted so synopsis lines can use list|add|done. Per-path flag validation is a future refinement.

docs.title: Status
docs.summary: Entry point after the autonomous iteration: what works, what is pinned, and what waits for a human decision.
docs.body_html:
Snapshot · 2026-10-23

niuse is runnable end to end: seven Markdown stores, an interactive REPL with line editing, history, completion, multi-line input, confirmation and conflict handling, the in-band protocol, a read-only startup brief, bootstrap from history (memory candidates and a user profile), JSON views for every store, one-shot session listing, colored approval diffs, doctor, and acceptance metrics. The declared MSRV is 1.88; the full test suite and the optional tui feature pass under it, and a weekly workflow checks both.

Both repositories are green. The board at https://niuverse.github.io/niuse/ is deployed from a single generated file; source docs are not published. niuse builds against the niucode revision in niucode.rev. The long-running direction is in roadmap: harness-native companion, compounding context, long-horizon work, connected tools, and proof.

Verify
