./scripts/check.sh              # fmt, clippy, docs, tests, package, dashboard
./scripts/check-niucode-drift.sh
cargo xtask dashboard --check
cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace --all-targets   # MSRV, also run weekly

Works

  • niuse REPL: streaming, slash commands, line editing and history, Tab completion for commands/ids/paths, backslash continuation, /new chapters, /cd, /model, /cost, /threads, /sessions, /resume, /export, /brief, /plan, candidate confirm/edit/skip, conflict replace/keep.
  • Brief: niuse brief [--json], /brief in the REPL and TUI, and a compact actionable block after the banner; no provider call and NIUSE_BRIEF=off restores the quiet start.
  • Projects: niuse projects [--limit N] [--all] [--json] reads niucode's recorded workspaces, sorts by recent activity, hides missing and temporary test checkouts by default, and shows the current project in status.
  • Digest: niuse digest [--thread PATH] [--dry-run] [--limit N] compresses recent user/assistant prose into at most five journal bullets with one tool-free model call; tool output never enters the prompt, secrets refuse the whole write, and the path stays opt-in until ten real digests are reviewed.
  • niuse tui (optional feature): niucode's TUI with CompanionHooks; protocol stripping, journal/loops, memory accept/edit/replace/keep, read-only commands, /brief, /goals, /plan, /recall, /export, y/n/s approval keys, and /cost read from the thread event log.
  • MCP: every path mounts read-only servers from NIUSE_MCP_CONFIG or ~/.niucode/mcp.toml; a broken manifest warns and disables MCP for that run. The notes pack (packs/notes) exposes search/read/list over NOTES_DIR and refuses path escapes; the calendar pack (packs/calendar) lists and searches one ICS file without network or timezone conversion. niuse mcp init installs both packs, writes a read-only manifest, and merges new servers into an existing manifest by name without losing comments; --force replaces it. A PTY test drives the TUI mount and an MCP tool call through the replay provider.
  • Memory: search including expired entries, kind filter, kind counts, show/edit, review with metrics, prune with backup and freed-byte report, duplicate guard, secret scan, soft expiry.
  • Evidence: niuse evidence [--thread PATH] [--json] and /evidence report tool calls, write/edit paths, test-like bash checks, recorded verifications, delegated subagent runs (including unfinished ones), failures, and denied approvals without claiming correctness. niuse verify -- <command> and /verify <command> run a check and append a verification event.
  • Recall: niuse recall <query> [--json] and /recall search memory (including expired), journal, loops, and goals together; the agent can also call the read-only memory_search tool during a turn, and the protocol tells it to request /recall when no tool is available.
  • Dates: journal, memory, and stats day labels follow the local calendar; event timestamps stay UTC.
  • Journal and loops: model-written blocks plus manual entry and manual promises.
  • Plan: plan.md holds human-owned steps with p-N labels; open steps are injected after goals and before memory. niuse plan list|add|done edits them, and done refuses without a passing verification event tagged with that step. The REPL and TUI expose /steps (list/add/done); the TUI also has /verify p-N <command> over the same gate, with a PTY regression for the full flow. niuse evidence shows each step's verification status.
  • Goals: goals.md holds human-owned outcomes with g- ids; niuse goals list|add|done and /goals edit them, at most seven open, secret-scanned, and injected after user and before memory.
  • Bootstrap: dry-run preview, candidate merge into the inbox, optional user.md draft.
  • Sessions: derived thread titles, threads and sessions listings, Markdown export with a title, JSON output.
  • Machine output: JSON for memory (list/search/show), journal, threads, sessions, loops, status, doctor, stats, config effective, identity, and user; stats totals and trends include token usage, cache-hit percent, and tokens per turn.
  • Operations: pinned niucode revision, contract tests, nightly main check, doctor, acceptance metrics.
  • Distribution: niuse/niuse-core 0.1.12 and the eight niucode-* crates 0.1.6 are published. cargo package -p niuse passes against the registry; a clean-root cargo install niuse --version 0.1.12 --locked reports niuse 0.1.12. M3 is done; the 0.1.12 release page records the preflight and the retry.

Stage

Stage report · 2026-10-23 records what is proven, the open gates, and the decisions waiting on a human.

Waiting on you

  1. Dogfood — ten working days recorded in dogfood; started 2026-10-22 at 1/10 with a real read-only exec turn (README.md:106 citation, 11k in / 76 out / 3.5k cached) a real MCP turn (mcp__notes__search_notes found launch.md, 5k in / 95 out / 3.1k cached), a real TUI turn (391, 13k in / 2 out), a real approved write in a scratch workspace (3 steps, 7.1k in / 279 out / 6.3k cached), a real NIUSE_MEMORY=off A/B (on cited m-3d0b; off said NO_INJECTED_MEMORY), and one recorded disagreement: the companion argued against a third RSS pack and I dropped it. 2026-10-23 is 2/10: a real TUI task read DAY_TWO_C.md (27k in / 47 out / 13.4k cached) after the missing TUI on_turn_end metric was fixed. niuse dogfood --file docs/dogfood.md --note "..." (or ./scripts/dogfood.sh "note") writes the day's row from metrics; niuse report --days 7 (also /report [days] in the REPL and TUI) assembles turns, tokens/cache, open goals/promises/plan, and dogfood progress; niuse doctor shows the active-day count; scripts/dogfood-check.sh --complete checks the table and criteria. Only real use and review can close M2.
  2. TUI dogfood — ten real days on niuse tui for M5-002; this is also the ADR-0004 gate for retiring the REPL renderer.

Milestones

  • M5 · Harness-native companion — active. M5-001 is done: configurable y/n/s approval keys, an offline PTY deny/allow test, product commands in TUI help/completion, and /cost computed from the thread event log. M5-002 is 2/10 TUI days after real TUI turns on 2026-10-22 (391, 13k in / 2 out) and 2026-10-23 (27k in / 47 out / 13.4k cached); eight distinct working days remain. The shared TUI now renders inline Markdown (bold, italic, code, links, headings), pipe tables as box-drawing blocks, common TeX math as Unicode, lists/tasks/quotes, code fences replaced by a language label, display math rendered without $$ fences, a streaming caret/per-tool timer in the activity footer, and niucode web --session serves a loopback-only read-only viewer with a live SSE tail a read-only browser prompt, streaming deltas in the web client, and browser approvals, and server-rendered Markdown and native MathML in the web transcript; the raw event log is unchanged. /new (alias of /clear) and /reset both archive the old thread and reset thread.jsonl through niucode's new-session seam; /resume and /fork now notify the hooks too; PTY tests prove /verify after /resume and /fork writes to the live session, the after-turn memory prompt can accept or discard, and /brief, /report, and /steps compose in one session. Cross-restart active-thread semantics are decided in ADR-0007: /resume and /fork are session-scoped; thread.jsonl stays the only active line.

  • M6 · Compounding context — done. Brief, project registry, unified recall, and memory_search landed. The digest reached 10/10 real reviews; NONE, old-loop reminders, restated memory, and failed-then-fixed checks are handled, every verdict prints a reason, and the digest stays opt-in by choice.

  • M7 · Long-horizon work — done. Goals, plan mode, evidence, recorded verification, verification-gated steps, open-plan injection, and delegated-run evidence all landed; a real model respected the gate and refused to close a step without evidence. The next product phase is M8 connected agent and M9 proof.

  • M10 · Web companion — active. niuse web --features web serves the browser surface with the identity/memory/plan system prompt and a product sidebar over niucode's SSE, approval, Markdown, and MathML code. The feature is opt-in so the default binary still does not link niucode. The sidebar shows identity/user/goals/plan/memory/loops plus a bounded 7-day report (including dogfood), alongside model/policy status and a live SSE turn timer. The shared TUI now covers ordered lists, horizontal rules, and bold table headers with dim borders and inline styles inside table cells.

  • M8 · Connected agent — done. niucode ships the stdio MCP client with explicit trust, timeouts, and metadata; niuse mounts it in the TUI, REPL, and exec, and ships notes/calendar packs. ADR-0034 is implemented: write_tools, --allow-mcp-write, interactive mount gating, per-call approval with a bounded argument preview, shared write lock, no retry, and no subagent inheritance. The notes pack has opt-in create_note; driver, agent, and TUI tests cover deny/allow, the TUI PTY proves the preview and both outcomes, and /evidence shows each mount's server, write allowlist, and config hash.

  • M9 · Proof — ./scripts/eval.sh covers memory-on/off A/B, goal and plan injection, the startup brief, agent recall, the notes and calendar MCP packs, MCP timeout/read-only refusal, prompt-size budgets, a stable cache-prefix invariant, a combined two-pack + plan + verification workflow, multi-turn step execution where closed steps leave the next prompt, and the failed-verification recovery path. scripts/dogfood-trend.sh compares two weeks of real use and blocks publish-niuse.sh on a regression; scripts/check-links.py keeps the docs' relative links honest; scripts/check-board.py rejects done milestones with open cards, doing cards in planned milestones, and missing blocked reasons; README CLI examples and flags are checked against clap in the test suite.

  • M2 dogfood is in progress: 2/10 days, acceptance 100% (1/1), three distinct cited memory ids and one disagreement so far. The real 2026-10-23 retrieval cited m-f356, m-5c68, and m-3d0b; the day is also TUI day 2/10. It still decides whether the memory layer pays for itself.

Not built

Daemon, web UI, messaging bridges, scheduled push, vector search, full session indexing, automatic repo edits, and multi-user support remain out until a new ADR. The TUI is opt-in, not the default; see roadmap for the order.

docs.title: ADR-0004：Renderer migration waits for TUI dogfood
docs.summary: Keep the rustyline REPL and its renderer as the default; TUI is opt-in until ten real TUI dogfood days and parity are proven.
docs.body_html:
背景

ADR-0032 的 TUI seam 已经落地：niucode 0.1.5 提供 prompt / event / turn-end / filter / command / commands / after_turn hooks；niuse 0.1.11 的 tui feature 通过这些 hooks 跑通了协议剥离、journal/loops、memory 确认、审批 allow/deny、只读命令和 /export。

但 niuse 的默认入口仍是 rustyline REPL；render.rs 仍在服务它。现在删掉 renderer 会让默认路径失去经过最多真实使用的界面，也会把产品 UI 一次性绑到上游 TUI 的演进节奏上。

决策

  1. 默认仍是 REPL + render.rs。 TUI 是显式的 tui feature，发布为可选安装。
  2. 不搬文件。 renderer 删除发生在真实使用证明 TUI 路径之后，而不是在代码看起来可复用之后。
  3. 删除门槛：
    • 十个真实工作日的 TUI dogfood，每天至少一个真实任务；
    • 审批 allow/deny、memory accept/edit/replace/keep、NIUSE_MEMORY=off、/export 都无回归；
    • 至少一次 TUI 会话中 candidate 被接受并在一周后仍被正确引用；
    • 默认安装仍能只装 REPL，TUI 依赖不进入默认二进制。
  4. 期间允许的改动：只修 TUI 行为与 seam，不把新的产品逻辑写进 niucode。

备选

方案否决理由
立刻删除 render.rs，TUI 转为默认默认路径的回归面最大，dogfood 数据不足
永久保留两套 renderer长期双维护；ADR-0032 的收益无法兑现
把 TUI 变成默认、REPL 变 feature改变已发布默认行为，用户没有要求

后果

  • 短期保留两套前端，成本是已知的；
  • TUI 的每次改进都可以独立验证，不赌默认路径；
  • 删除 renderer 是一个有明确验收的可回退决定，而不是仓库整理动作。

验收

  • TUI 为 opt-in feature，默认二进制不链接 TUI。
  • TUI 的 hooks 和确认路径有 PTY/单元测试。
  • 十个真实 TUI dogfood 日。
  • 删除 renderer 的独立提交。

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: niuse boundaries, the seven stores, turn data flow, write thresholds, and explicit non-goals.
docs.body_html:
In one sentence

niuse is the identity and memory layer above niucode: it decides who the companion is, what it remembers, and what it promised. Whether a task can be done at all stays with niucode's loop, tools, and sandbox.

Dependency direction

crates/niuse-cli     REPL / commands / renderer / driver / bootstrap
    │
crates/niuse-core    date / model / store / prompt / candidate / policy
    │
niucode-agent        run_with_history / AgentConfig / project_history
niucode-core         SessionLog / Event
niucode-provider     Provider / ChatMessage
niucode-auth         AuthStore
niucode-tools        SandboxPolicy / ApprovalMode

Only driver.rs and memory_tool.rs touch niucode-agent directly. Everything else is either pure domain logic or only knows niuse-core types. When niucode upgrades, the required changes are confined to those adapters.

niuse does not fork niucode and does not add a memory hook to its loop. Memory is a product layer; the kernel stays minimal.

niucode exposes a read-only EmbedderTool seam (ADR-0032): niuse registers memory_search through it in the REPL, exec, and TUI. The tool reuses unified recall, is advertised as read-only, and cannot write, delete, or confirm memory.

niucode now exposes a library target and the generic TurnHooks trait (ADR-0032). Both run_exec_with_hooks and run_tui_with_hooks invoke prompt, event, and turn-end hooks; the renderer migration remains. niuse keeps its REPL and renderer deliberately rather than accidentally until that migration lands.

Terminal input uses rustyline only when stdin is a TTY; pipes keep the plain reader. History is stored at ~/.niuse/history with mode 0600. A line ending in \ continues the prompt and is joined into one user message.

Modules

ModuleLayerResponsibility
cliInterfaceflags, subcommands, offline commands, wiring
replInterfaceconversation, slash commands, candidate confirmation, rendering
promptEnginestable-prefix system prompt and budgets
briefEngineread-only "what needs attention" view over the stores
protocolEnginein-band block parsing and streaming stripping
policyEnginesoft expiry, conflicts, secret scanning
driverAdaptersniucode boundary, sessions, per-turn cwd
projectsAdaptersread-only view of niucode's project registry
bootstrapAdaptersold-session mining and the inbox
storesStateseven-store load / save and permissions
dashboardEngineeringoffline board generation

Active thread

thread.jsonl is the only active line across restarts; threads/*.jsonl are archived chapters. TUI /resume and /fork switch the live session for that run and notify embedder hooks, but they do not change the file the next launch opens. /new and /reset archive the current line and start a new thread.jsonl. See ADR-0007.

Turn data flow

startup
  ├─ read identity / user / memory / loops / journal
  ├─ compose() assembles the system prompt (once per session)
  ├─ brief: overdue loops, inbox, stale/expired memory (read-only)
  └─ project_history(thread.jsonl) restores history

user input
  ├─ run_with_history(config, prompt, history)
  ├─ AgentEvent → Renderer (TextDelta goes through StreamFilter)
  ├─ trailing buffer strips <<niuse:*>> blocks
  ├─ journal / loop: written automatically
  ├─ memory: print candidate → y / n / e / s
  └─ re-project history, next turn

There is no second copy of the conversation. niuse export renders the event log as Markdown without changing it. history is projected from the event log by niucode's project_history, so compaction, replay, and fork behave exactly as they do in niucode.

The seven stores and injection

~/.niuse/
  identity.md      who it is (human-written; it may only propose)
  user.md          who you are (bootstrapped with --profile, human-reviewed)
  memory/          facts: preferences, decisions, pitfalls (confirmed, expiring)
  journal/         experience: one file per month, merged per day (automatic)
  loops.md         promises (automatic, optional due date)
  goals.md         human-owned outcomes (injected, at most seven open)
  plan.md          human-owned steps (open ones injected; closed only with verification)
  thread.jsonl     the relationship thread
  threads/         archived chapters from `/new`
  sessions/        one-shot `exec` logs (`niuse sessions`)
  inbox.md         bootstrap review queue
  history          TTY prompt history (0600)
  backups/         prune snapshots (0700)
  metrics.jsonl    local acceptance counters
  config.toml      defaults and overrides

Defaults come from CLI flags, then ~/.niuse/config.toml, then built-ins; only commands that build a provider read the file.

Injection order is fixed, stable before volatile:

SectionBudgetChange rate
personaconstantnever
identity≤ 600 tokvery low
user≤ 600 toklow
goals≤ 300 toklow
memory≤ 2 000 toklow
protocolconstantnever
todayone linedaily
loops≤ 300 tokmedium
journal≤ 600 tokhigh

The first five sections form the stable cache prefix; only content after today can vary per session. The system prompt is assembled once and is not rebuilt mid-session. identity.md is the only source of the companion's name and voice; the persona describes working style and the product name is not a self-name. When identity is missing, the prompt says so explicitly instead of inventing a name.

Write thresholds and protocol

WhatWho decidesConfirmation
journal, loopsthe companionnone
memoryit proposesrequired
identitythe humanonly the human can change it

The model may end an answer with three block types:

<<niuse:memory kind=preference tags=rust,testing>>
one self-contained conclusion
<</niuse:memory>>

<<niuse:loop due=2026-10-22>>
something it promised to do
<</niuse:loop>>

<<niuse:journal>>
- a decision or turning point that differs from last time
<</niuse:journal>>

At most one memory block per turn; after a rejection, the same tags are not proposed again in that session. journal records changes, not activity logs. Expired memory leaves the prompt but stays searchable through niuse mem search and /mem recall.

Safety and privacy

  • ~/.niuse directories are 0700, files are 0600. Writers create the file at 0600 from the first byte (unique temp name, then rename); a chmod only repairs pre-existing files. $EDITOR scratch files, exports, and thread logs follow the same rule.
  • mem prune --apply copies memory files to ~/.niuse/backups/ before deleting.
  • Secret patterns are scanned before every write; a match is refused, and the CLI requires --force to override where an override exists.
  • identity.md and user.md edits, and the bootstrap profile draft, are refused on a secret match; these files are injected every turn.
  • Manual mem add runs the same conflict rule as candidates; --force overrides both the secret and duplicate checks.
  • Approval renders niucode's structured change preview (hunks, capped at 80 lines) before asking.
  • Memory is sent to the provider on every turn, so the leak surface is larger than a normal file.
  • Project knowledge stays in the repo's AGENTS.md; niuse never edits your repositories.
  • NIUSE_MEMORY=off disables injection and candidates, for A/B runs and for recovering trust.
  • niuse doctor checks home permissions, identity, credentials, bwrap, and the pinned niucode revision without calling a model.
  • metrics.jsonl records local counters only: turn outcomes, candidate decisions, tags, and ids. Memory text never enters it.

Explicit non-goals

A daemon, a web UI, WeChat / Feishu bridges, scheduled push notifications, vector search, full session indexing, automatic repo edits, and multi-user support. The TUI is opt-in until ADR-0004's gate.

ADR-0005 widens the product scope: project awareness, briefs, goals, delegation, and connectors are allowed when they serve one person and stay terminal-first. The test for every proposal is still: does this help the companion finish real work without making the system harder to trust?

docs.title: Implementation plan
docs.summary: Fifteen decisions, the seven stores, turn lifecycle, write thresholds, milestones, and verifiable acceptance.
docs.body_html:
In one sentence

Add a persistent identity and memory layer above niucode so the same agent knows you across projects and sessions. No resident service, no vector search, no automatic edits to your repositories.

1. Positioning

niucode owns "can do": loop, tools, sandbox, event log. niuse owns "who": what it remembers, what it promised, and when it should disagree with you.

One test decides whether a feature belongs here: does it shape an identity, or is it just another capability? Capabilities stay in niucode or are not built.

2. Decisions

#QuestionDecision
D1PositioningCross-project engineering memory
D2ContentPreferences, decisions, pitfalls; few, high-value, reviewable
D3OwnershipGlobal preferences in niuse; project knowledge in the repo's AGENTS.md
D4WritingThe agent proposes, one key confirms; at most one per turn
D5ReadingFull injection filtered by scope
D6ArchitectureSeparate repo, depends on niucode libs, drives turns itself
D7Storage~/.niuse/, plain Markdown, 0600
D8InterfaceInteractive REPL; TUI deferred
D9ExpirySoft expiry, replace on conflict
D10PrivacySecret-pattern blacklist, refuse on match
D11MVPOnly the global-preference loop
D12Top riskConfirmation fatigue
D13ShapeIdentity layer plus resumable session, no resident process
D14Cold startMine history; you define identity
D15CharacterAn opinionated collaborator

Rationale for each trade-off lives in ADR-0001 and ADR-0002.

Admission criteria for memory

A piece of information may enter memory/ only if all three hold:

  1. It is still useful across sessions.
  2. It cannot be found by grep in the repository.
  3. It fits in one sentence a human can review.

Anything else is rejected. This is what keeps "index every session" and "environment facts" out: they look like memory but are really retrieval and configuration.

3. Stores and injection

3.1 The seven stores

~/.niuse/
  identity.md          who it is: name, voice, values, boundaries
  user.md              who you are: goals, rhythm, taste, red lines, current work
  memory/
    preferences.md
    lessons.md         decisions and pitfalls
  journal/
    2026-10.md         experience, one file per month
  loops.md             promises: things it said it would do
  goals.md             human-owned outcomes (ADR-0006)
  plan.md              human-owned steps; open ones injected, verification-gated completion
  • UTF-8 Markdown only; directories 0700, files 0600.
  • memory/ may be its own git repository for backup and diffs; journal/ is not committed by default.
  • No database. For a single user and under 200 entries, files are the best query engine.

3.2 Injection order and budget

Stable before volatile; the system prompt is assembled once per session (never rebuilt mid-session, to avoid a cache miss on every turn):

SectionSourceBudgetChange rate
Identityidentity.md≤ 600 tokvery low
Useruser.md≤ 600 toklow
Factsmemory/*.md≤ 2 000 toklow
Promisesloops.md≤ 300 tokmedium
Recent experiencelast 3 journal/ days≤ 600 tokhigh

About 4k tokens in total. Over budget, drop the oldest unverified facts first, then truncate the journal; never silently drop identity or user.

3.3 Entry format

One memory is one section: machine-parseable and human-readable.

### m-7f3a

- Conclusion: Rust repositories use `cargo nextest`, never `cargo test`
- Tags: rust, testing
- Created: 2026-10-21
- Last confirmed: 2026-10-21
- Source: `1792493790852-350850-0`

id is four random hex digits and is never reused. Source points at the niucode session id and is the only audit trail.

loops.md:

- [ ] l-7f3a Confirm whether niucode supports per-turn cwd (due 2026-10-22)
- [x] l-91cc Cap the bootstrap sample (2026-10-21)

4. Turn lifecycle

startup
  ├─ read the six injected stores
  ├─ assemble the system prompt (once)
  └─ restore thread history via project_history

each input
  ├─ run_with_history(config, prompt, history)
  ├─ stream events (own renderer)
  ├─ tail buffer: strip <<niuse:memory>> / <<niuse:loop>> / <<niuse:journal>> blocks
  ├─ candidate? print it → y / n / e
  ├─ accept → write memory (or loops)
  └─ append to the journal buffer

exit / project switch
  └─ journal is already on disk

history is projected by niucode's project_history from session events; there is no second copy of the conversation. Replay, fork, and compaction therefore behave exactly as in niucode, and niuse does not reinvent them.

5. Write thresholds

5.1 Candidate protocol

No extra model call. The system prompt states that the model may append a block when a turn produced something durable:

<<niuse:memory kind=preference tags=rust,testing>>
Rust repositories use cargo nextest, never cargo test
<</niuse:memory>>

Rules:

  • At most one block per turn; if there is nothing, say nothing. Long runs without a candidate are normal.
  • Only memory and loop and journal blocks are recognised.
  • After a memory rejection, the same tags are not proposed again in that session.
  • A parse failure counts as "no candidate": no error, no guessing.

The cost is that the model may miss things. Missing is acceptable; recording something wrong is not — the same value as D9. If dogfooding shows serious under-recording after two weeks, add an offline proposer then, not now.

5.2 Confirmation

Memory candidate [global · rust,testing]
  Rust repositories use cargo nextest, never cargo test
  [y] accept   [n] discard   [e] edit   [s] stop proposing this session

e opens $EDITOR. A conflict does not overwrite silently:

Conflicts with m-91cc:
  old: Rust projects use cargo test
  new: Rust repositories use cargo nextest
  [r] replace   [k] keep both   [d] discard

5.3 Journal

Written automatically, no confirmation, but only under strict rules:

  • Three to five lines, only what differs from last time: decisions, turning points, open questions, mood shifts.
  • No activity logs ("fixed a bug today"), no duplication of memory/.
  • Events and judgements only, not code detail. Paths may be referenced; code is not copied.
  • Scanned for secrets before writing, since transcripts may contain keys.

The journal is not a log; it is compressed shared experience. The test: read it three months later and see whether the trade-off comes back.

5.4 Loops

  • When it says "I'll check next time" or "I'll follow up", that goes into loops.md; otherwise trust erodes.
  • Each entry may carry a due date; every open entry is injected, with the earliest due date first.
  • Closing a loop needs evidence (a verification, a conclusion), not a feeling of completion.

6. Expiry, conflicts, privacy

6.1 Soft expiry

Age since last confirmedInjection behaviour
≤ 30 daysinjected normally
31–90 daysinjected, marked (unverified since YYYY-MM-DD)
> 90 daysnot injected automatically; visible via /mem recall

No automatic deletion. Deletion is irreversible and you would never know what it removed. /mem review supports bulk re-confirmation and cleanup.

journal is exempt from expiry: experience does not become invalid, only old. loops uses due dates, not age.

6.2 Conflicts

Before writing, a new memory is compared with the existing store:

  • normalise (lowercase, strip punctuation), take character bigrams, Jaccard ≥ 0.5 is a likely conflict;
  • same tag and similarity ≥ 0.35 also counts;
  • a hit opens replace / keep both / discard; never merge automatically.

The 0.5 threshold is a starting point and will be adjusted after two weeks of false positives. No embeddings: at 200 entries the complexity outweighs the benefit.

6.3 Privacy

Memory is sent to the provider every turn, so leaked content leaks far more often than in an ordinary file. Every write is scanned; a hit is refused with a reason:

PatternExample
sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}OpenAI / DeepSeek key
ghp_ / github_pat_GitHub token
AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}AWS access key
-----BEGIN .* PRIVATE KEY-----private key
xox[baprs]-Slack token
32+ hex / base64 rungeneric key shape

Scanning is a backstop, not a guarantee. Private projects, client names, and internal addresses still depend on human judgement at confirmation time. NIUSE_MEMORY=off disables injection entirely, for A/B runs and trust recovery.

7. Cold start

niuse bootstrap turns history into user.md and memory candidates once:

  1. Enumerate ~/.niucode/sessions/*.jsonl, last 90 days, at most 40, most recently modified first.
  2. Send only user / assistant text, dropping tool output, through one tool-free extraction that returns {kind, text, tags}.
  3. Deduplicate, group by kind, and write ~/.niuse/inbox.md with the source session id on every line.
  4. niuse review walks the queue: y accept, e edit, n discard, s skip for the next run, q quit.
  5. With --profile, one extra call drafts user.md from the same sessions when the file is missing; --force-profile overwrites.
  6. identity.md is not mined: niuse identity init asks eight questions, records your answers, and lets you edit them.

Cost estimate: 40 sessions × about 2k input tokens ≈ 100k tokens, one-off.

Mining boundary: only the three kinds from D2. No code facts, no environment configuration, no information about other people.

8. Architecture

crates/niuse-cli     REPL, commands, renderer, driver, bootstrap
    │
crates/niuse-core    date / model / store / prompt / candidate / policy
    │
niucode-agent        run_with_history / AgentConfig / project_history
niucode-core         SessionLog / Event
niucode-provider / auth / tools
  • Two crates: niuse-core depends only on anyhow and regex, and its tests need no API key; niuse-cli owns the terminal, provider wiring, and driver.
  • The dependency points at a sibling checkout via path plus version = "0.1.0". The chosen path is to publish the niucode crates first; until the upload exists, a fresh machine still needs the sibling checkout or the pinned revision.
  • A NiucodeDriver-style seam (about 200 lines) isolates API churn: config assembly, history projection, event forwarding.
  • At MVP time niucode-cli had no library target, so niuse wrote a minimal renderer. ADR-0032 has since added the library target and exported TurnHooks; invoking those hooks and migrating the renderer remain.
  • No changes to niucode's loop, no memory hook in the kernel. Memory is a product layer; the kernel stays minimal.

9. Three assumptions verified in W1

Written down is not verified. Each was tested in the first week; if any had failed, the design would have changed.

  1. Per-turn cwd on one session — passes: reading in one directory, /cd /tmp, reading in another, both succeed in the same thread.jsonl, with history rebuilt correctly.
  2. Reliable stripping of trailing candidate blocks in a stream — passes: the filter covers blocks split across chunks, partial prefixes, false markers, and unterminated blocks; real calls show the block removed and the prose intact.
  3. niucode-agent's public API fits a thin adapter — passes: driver.rs is about 200 lines with nothing to fork or bypass. The only thing written from scratch is the renderer, because niucode-cli has no library target.

10. Milestones

WeekDeliverableStatus
W1Three spikes; crate skeleton; five-store reads/writes; prompt assembly; one real turn in the REPLdone
W2Candidate block and confirmation; journal; loops; soft expiry; secret scandone
W3niuse bootstrap; dogfood; acceptance databootstrap and review done; dogfood pending

11. Acceptance

Technical checks passed on 2026-10-21: five-store reads/writes and 0600, candidate protocol, streaming strip, soft expiry, secret scan, the full bootstrap → review → memory chain, per-turn cwd in one session, and cargo xtask dashboard --check.

What remains is product acceptance, which requires real use:

  • Ten consecutive working days, at least one real task per day through niuse
  • Candidate acceptance rate ≥ 60% (accepted / proposed)
  • At least 3 cases where it cites a past judgement and the citation is correct
  • At least 1 case where it disagrees and you change your mind
  • Memory store ≤ 50 entries (more means the bar is too low)
  • At least 1 A/B case where NIUSE_MEMORY=off produces a different answer

The last item is the anti-placebo check: if turning memory off changes nothing, the layer has no reason to exist.

12. Non-goals

Daemon, web UI, WeChat / Feishu bridges, scheduled push, vector search, full session indexing, automatic repo edits, multi-user support, and a general agent framework.

Update 2026-10-22: ADR-0005 revises this list. A terminal-first working companion — project awareness, briefs, goals, delegation, and connectors — is now in scope. Daemon, web UI, scheduled push, vector search, automatic repo edits, and multi-user support still require a new ADR; the TUI is opt-in until ADR-0004's gate.

13. Risks

RiskSymptomMitigation
Confirmation fatigue (top)Blind y presses, then the feature is switched offAt most one per turn; no repeated tags after rejection; observable acceptance rate; NIUSE_MEMORY=off
Persona performanceLines like "I missed you"Hard rules in identity.md; companionship rests on memory, promises, disagreement
Journal becomes an activity log"Fixed a bug today"Only changes and judgements; monthly review removes empty entries
Dependency rotniucode moves and the build breaksPin the revision; thin adapter; upstream a library split if needed
Cold-start noise"User likes clean code" × 20Only three kinds; every candidate carries a source; batch review, not accept-all

14. Open questions

  • Its name: niuse is the project name, not necessarily what you call it; define that in identity.md.
  • Bootstrap sample size and cost: decide after one real run.
  • Whether it may propose changes to identity.md: proposal yes, confirmation required.
  • Session model beyond a single thread: /new, per-project sessions; wait for real usage to expose the need.

15. Implementation map and deviations

Implemented in crates/niuse-core and crates/niuse-cli:

Plan itemLocation
Five stores, 0600store.rs, atomic write plus chmod
Injection and budgetsprompt.rs, stable sections first
Protocol blocks and streaming stripcandidate.rs, six boundary tests
Soft expiry / conflicts / secret scanpolicy.rs plus prompt.rs
REPL, confirmation, /mem and friendsrepl.rs, commands.rs
Session resume and per-turn cwddriver.rs
Cold startbootstrap.rs (bootstrap + review)
Architecture dashboardcrates/xtask plus docs/dashboard/project.json
Memory kill switchNIUSE_MEMORY=off in repl.rs

Deviations and later additions:

  1. A third protocol block, journal. The plan had memory and loop only; to avoid an extra model call, the main model emits a journal block and niuse writes it automatically.
  2. exec never writes memory. It prints candidates to stderr so scripted calls cannot change the store silently.
  3. Approval shows a unified diff. The preview is capped at 80 lines and d prints the full diff before the y/N decision; denial still returns the structured preview to the model. The earlier summary-only limitation is resolved.

docs.body_html:
North star

A personal engineering agent that knows the person, the projects, and the work in flight; it can plan, act, delegate, and return evidence. It still runs in the terminal, stores what it knows as files, and keeps the kernel generic.

The test for a feature is no longer only "does it shape an identity?". It is also: does it help the companion finish real work without making the system harder to trust?

Where we are

  • Identity, memory, loops, journal, soft expiry, conflicts, secret scanning, and a resumable thread work end to end.
  • The REPL is the default. niuse tui exists behind the tui feature and already runs niucode's goals, plans, subagents, skills, resume picker, and permission commands through CompanionHooks.
  • niucode 0.1.5 exposes the library, the hook surface, the command registry, /plan and /goal, subagents, skills, and the extension host.
  • The product gate is still dogfood; the old front end is still the default until ADR-0004's ten-day TUI gate is met.

The split

LayerOwnsDoes not own
niucodeloop, event log, providers, tools, sandbox, approvals, goals runtime, subagents, extension/MCP seamspersonal memory, identity, product commands, personal data
niuseidentity, user model, memory, journal, loops, project context, product UX, personal tool packsa second loop, a second event log, a second durable store

When a capability is generic, build it in niucode first and consume it through the pinned revision. When it is personal, keep it in niuse and test it offline.

Phases

The board allows one active milestone, and that slot stays with M2 · Dogfood until the memory layer proves itself. M5–M9 are implementation tracks: their cards can be ready or done while the gate is open. This is deliberate — the product keeps moving, but the board does not pretend the proof is finished.

M5 · Harness-native companion (active)

Goal: make the existing harness the companion's default working surface instead of maintaining a parallel front end.

Exit

  • niuse tui reaches approval-preview and usage parity with the REPL contract.
  • The product commands, /brief, /goal, /plan, and skills are discoverable in the TUI and covered by tests.
  • Ten real TUI dogfood days are recorded, one real task per day.
  • The renderer is retired only after that gate, per ADR-0004.

Cards: M5-001 done; M5-002 is 2/10 TUI days.

M6 · Compounding context (done)

Goal: make what the companion knows visible and useful at the moment work starts, without adding a database.

Exit

  • A startup brief surfaces overdue promises, review queues, and stale memory.
  • A project registry answers "what was I doing, and where?" across repositories.
  • A session digest turns a finished thread into a journal entry with evidence.
  • Memory has an explicit on-demand recall path beyond the injected budget.

Cards: M6-001 through M6-013; the phase is complete, digest stays opt-in.

M7 · Long-horizon work (done)

Goal: let one request become a checked sequence of work that survives a session boundary.

Exit

  • Product-level goals persist across sessions and are injected with their state.
  • A plan → execute → verify loop records each step and its evidence.
  • Delegation to subagents has a budget, a scope, and a summary the parent can audit.
  • A three-day goal completes without re-explaining the task.

Cards: M7-001 through M7-007; the phase is complete.

M8 · Connected agent (done)

Goal: reach personal tools and data through a standard, trust-bounded connector instead of one-off shell commands.

Exit

  • niucode ships a stdio MCP client with trust, timeouts, and tool metadata.
  • niuse ships at least one personal pack (for example notes or calendar) behind least privilege.
  • A connector cannot read credentials, escape its declared roots, or write without approval.

Cards: niucode M8-001 is done: read-only stdio v1 with explicit trust, config mounting in exec/TUI, and offline tests. niuse mounts the host in the TUI, REPL, and exec, ships read-only notes and calendar packs, installs both with niuse mcp init (which merges safely), and covers the TUI mount with a PTY test. ADR-0034 is accepted and implemented: write_tools, --allow-mcp-write, per-call approval, shared write lock, no retry. niuse exposes the flag, mounts writes only with an interactive terminal, ships an opt-in create_note notes tool, and the TUI PTY proves the preview plus deny/allow. M8 is complete.

M9 · Proof (planned)

Goal: measure whether the companion is actually more useful, and keep it that way.

Exit

  • An offline personal-agent suite covers memory recall, briefs, goals, and delegation.
  • A memory-on/off A/B case shows a behavioural difference.
  • Regressions in dogfood metrics block a release.

Cards: M9-001 through M9-006 are done: briefs, goals, memory A/B, recall, MCP boundaries, the dogfood trend gate, prompt-size budgets, token/cache signals, a combined two-pack workflow, multi-turn plan execution, and failed-verification recovery are covered.

The round ritual

  1. Read this file, status, and the chosen card.
  2. Implement the smallest complete behaviour; prefer a pure core function and a thin CLI/TUI adapter.
  3. Add the focused test the card promises; keep all tests offline.
  4. Update the card's status, updated, and completed; update status when the phase or the next action changes.
  5. Run cargo xtask dashboard and include the regenerated board.
  6. Run ./scripts/check.sh; commit and push only when it is green.
  7. Leave the next card and the next concrete action in status for the next round.

A round that only rewrites the plan does not count as progress unless it unblocks a card.

Guardrails

  • No daemon, web UI, scheduled push, vector index, or automatic repository edit without a new ADR.
  • No second durable store. The event log and the Markdown stores stay the truth.
  • No capability without a permission story: approval, sandbox, secret scan, or declared roots.
  • No silent memory write and no silent external write.
  • Kernel changes are generic and tested in niucode first; niuse never forks niucode files.
  • If the same blocker survives three rounds, mark it blocked with the concrete condition instead of looping.

Later, with an ADR

Background scheduling and notifications; a local web surface; vector or embedding recall; multi-user support; automatic edits to user repositories.

docs.title: ADR-0001: A global memory layer
docs.summary: Memory is a small global store, not a session index: plain Markdown, full injection, soft expiry, confirmation before writing; project knowledge stays in AGENTS.md.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-21. The W1 spike passed; the MVP is implemented in crates/niuse-core (store, policy, prompt, candidate).

Context

niucode already has AGENTS.md, skills, session resume, compaction, and fork, but it deliberately does not provide memory across sessions or projects (the roadmap lists it as deferred). The result: every new project starts by repeating preferences, decisions, and old pitfalls.

The obvious temptation is to index every session and retrieve from it. That direction has three concrete problems:

  1. Code facts are one grep away; indexing duplicates the repository.
  2. Retrieval quality needs an evaluation set, and niuse does not have one.
  3. Vectorising turns "reviewable" into "opaque": a wrong memory cannot be spotted at a glance.

Decision

  1. Memory is global, not per-session. It stores only what still holds across projects; project-level knowledge stays in the repository's AGENTS.md, and niuse never writes there automatically.
  2. Three kinds only: preferences, decisions, pitfalls. Admission requires: useful across sessions, not greppable in the repo, expressible in one reviewable sentence.
  3. Plain Markdown, under ~/.niuse/memory/, files 0600, optionally its own git repo. No SQLite, no JSONL.
  4. Full injection, filtered by scope, 2k-token budget. No query-time retrieval, so the system-prompt prefix stays stable and prompt caching survives.
  5. Confirmation before writing, at most one candidate per turn. The candidate is emitted in-band by the main model; no extra model call.
  6. Soft expiry: normal within 30 days, marked unverified from 31 to 90 days, not injected after 90. Never deleted automatically.
  7. Conflicts are never merged silently: lexical similarity above threshold offers replace / keep both / discard.
  8. Secret-pattern scan before writing; a match is refused. Memory is sent to the provider every turn, so the leak surface is much larger than an ordinary file.

Consequences

Better:

  • Memory is readable, editable, diffable, and revertible; mistakes are visible and fixable.
  • No retrieval dependency, works offline, no embedding service or evaluation set required.
  • The stable prompt prefix preserves the prompt-cache behaviour niucode relies on.

Worse:

  • A hard capacity limit around 200 entries; beyond that, manual merging or pruning is required.
  • Recall is "inject everything and let the model judge"; no relevance ranking, and too much memory dilutes attention.
  • Candidates depend on the main model volunteering them; missing one is normal.

Accepted trade-off: prefer missing a memory to recording a wrong one. A wrong memory enters every subsequent turn and is hard to notice; a missing one costs at most one repeated mistake.

Alternatives

OptionRejected because
Vector index over all sessionsNo evaluation set, not reviewable, duplicates grep, breaks the stable prefix
SQLite storageNo benefit at single-user, 200-entry scale; unreadable to humans and to diffs
Automatic distillationNoisy, and a wrong memory pollutes a turn before anyone can catch it; conflicts with "prefer missing"
Project memory in the global storeDuplicates AGENTS.md and drifts away from the code
Build it into the niucode kernelViolates niucode's minimal-harness boundary; memory should be a replaceable product layer

docs.title: ADR-0002: An identity layer, not a daemon
docs.summary: Identity is five Markdown stores, not prompt magic; companionship comes from memory, promises, and disagreement, not tone; what persists is the identity, not a process.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-21. The identity layer and REPL are implemented; journal and loops are written automatically from in-band protocol blocks.

Context

The goal is a personal companion, not a smarter tool. Two shapes exist in the ecosystem:

  • pi-memory style: IDENTITY.md / USER.md / MEMORY.md / daily/, injected at session start. Lightweight, but only a memory extension.
  • pi-durable-assistant style: a resident runtime, web UI, scheduled tasks, background subagents, a WeChat channel, and approval-gated memory. Heavy, and it turns a personal project into an operations project.

The cheap way to fake a companion is to give it a persona and a warm tone. That slides quickly into role-play: it talks a lot, remembers little, never disagrees, and does not improve your judgement.

Decision

  1. Identity is files, not prompt magic. identity.md, user.md, memory/, journal/, and loops.md are five persistent stores, all human-readable and editable. You can rewrite its values without touching code.
  2. You write the identity; it may only propose changes. History can mine user.md and memory candidates, but it cannot mine who it is.
  3. Injection order is stable-to-volatile: identity → user → memory → loops → recent journal. The system prompt is assembled once per session.
  4. Graded write thresholds: journal and loops are automatic; memory requires confirmation; identity is human-only.
  5. No daemon. No web UI, no WeChat, no scheduled push. It exists while the terminal is open and does not pretend to live in the background.
  6. Companionship rests on three things: remembering your judgements, tracking its own promises, and speaking up when you are wrong. Not emotional performance, not pet names, not spontaneous sentiment.
  7. It keeps a right to disagree. identity.md must state its judgement criteria and boundaries; disagreement comes with reasons, about the work rather than the person.
  8. The journal records change only. Three to five lines covering decisions, turning points, open questions, and shifts in mood; no activity logs, no duplication of memory.

Consequences

Better:

  • The identity is fully auditable: one git diff shows what changed about its character.
  • No operational burden: no servers, ports, certificates, or backup strategy.
  • Cold start can borrow history, so the first two weeks do not feel like meeting a stranger.

Worse:

  • It only exists while the terminal is open; it cannot remind you on a commute.
  • Without push, the freshness of loops depends on you opening the terminal.
  • Identity quality depends on whether you answer the eight questions; skip them and it degrades into a generic assistant.

Accepted trade-off: prove that "remembers, reliable, willing to disagree" is valuable before adding reach. Doing it the other way around produces a role-playing bot that interrupts you everywhere.

Alternatives

OptionRejected because
Resident daemon plus pushAbout five times the work, and it turns a personal project into an operations project; reach can come later
A persona paragraph in the system promptNot auditable, not revertible, and it drifts on every startup
Let the model self-update its identityIt slowly drifts toward pleasing you, which destroys the willingness to disagree
Reuse pi-durable-assistantA complete Node + SQLite runtime, incompatible with "built on niucode"
Rebuild the persona from memory each sessionNo shared history, nowhere for the journal to accumulate, no relationship to grow
docs.excerpt: Identity is five Markdown stores, not prompt magic; companionship comes from memory, promises, and disagreement, not tone; what persists is the identity, not a process.

docs.title: ADR-0003: niucode is the kernel and UI; niuse is the product
docs.summary: Keep two repositories. Upstream a reusable CLI library and turn hooks; niuse owns identity, memory, policy, and product defaults. Merge only if the product layer becomes thin enough that separate releases stop mattering.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-21.

Upstream proposal: niucode ADR-0032 · niuverse/niucode#1.

Context

At the time of writing, niuse drove niucode's turn loop itself and owned a small renderer, because niucode-cli was a binary with no library target. ADR-0032 has since added that library target and exported TurnHooks; the hook invocation and renderer migration are still ahead. Reusing niucode's TUI would remove the duplicate front end, which raises the obvious question: if niuse reuses the TUI, why not merge it into niucode?

Two facts make the merge tempting:

  • The shared surface is large: loop, session, tools, renderer, approval UI, diff preview.
  • Every shared change currently costs a revision bump and a contract test.

Two facts push the other way:

  • niucode's positioning is a minimal, observable coding harness that deliberately refuses long-term memory, resident services, and product defaults. Merging a companion into that repo changes what niucode is.
  • The two projects have different release cadences and different failure modes: kernel breakage versus product annoyance.

Decision

  1. Keep two repositories. niucode is the kernel and the reference UI; niuse is the product layer and the identity.
  2. Move the front end upstream, not the product. niucode-cli should expose a reusable library (TUI, runtime entry) plus a small turn-hook surface:
    • augment the system prompt before a turn;
    • observe a finished turn (for candidate extraction);
    • receive session lifecycle events. niuse implements the hooks and deletes its own renderer once the shared TUI is usable.
  3. Keep the product in niuse: identity, user model, memory, journal, loops, protocol blocks, expiry/conflict/privacy policy, product defaults (model, permissions, persona).
  4. Pin what you consume. niucode.rev fixes the revision required CI and deployments build against. The pin moves at most weekly through scripts/sync-niucode.sh; a nightly job tests niucode main so drift is visible early.
  5. Upstream first. Any capability that a generic niucode user would want lands in niucode first. niuse never forks kernel files.
  6. Set a merge trigger instead of debating forever. After the library split lands, if niuse's product-only surface falls below roughly 1,000 lines and separate releases stop mattering, merging becomes reasonable. Until then, two repos buy a clean kernel story and independent cadence.

Consequences

Better:

  • Reusing the TUI removes the largest duplication without diluting niucode's positioning.
  • The contract test plus pinned revision turns "did upstream break us?" into a CI signal.
  • Product decisions and kernel decisions keep separate ADR trails and release notes.

Worse:

  • niucode must grow a library API and hooks, which is real design work and must stay generic.
  • niuse still carries a binary, product defaults, and the hook implementation.
  • The weekly bump is a recurring chore, even if a small one.

Accepted trade-off: a little ceremony now beats either a fork or a premature monorepo. If the ceremony stops paying for itself, the merge trigger is explicit.

Alternatives

OptionRejected because
Merge niuse into niucode nowChanges what niucode is, couples releases, and mixes two boards and two audiences before the boundary is settled
Add --profile personal to niucodeHides a product inside the kernel; the personal layer would inherit kernel release pressure and vice versa
Fork niucode inside niuseDuplicates the loop and the front end, and guarantees drift
Keep the duplicate renderer foreverCheapest this month, most expensive this year; every TUI improvement has to be rebuilt twice
docs.excerpt: Keep two repositories. Upstream a reusable CLI library and turn hooks; niuse owns identity, memory, policy, and product defaults. Merge only if the product layer becomes thin enough that separate releases stop mattering.

docs.title: ADR-0005: A working companion, not only a memory layer
docs.summary: niuse stays terminal-first and file-based, but grows project awareness, proactive briefs, long-horizon goals, and delegation. Generic capabilities land in niucode first.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-22. This revises the non-goals in plan §12 and D8 (TUI deferred). ADR-0003 still governs the kernel/product split, and ADR-0004 still gates removing the renderer.

Context

The MVP proved the memory loop: identity, confirmed memory, automatic journal and loops, soft expiry, secret scanning, and a resumable thread. The remaining product gate is dogfood, not another store.

A companion that can only remember is a diary. The useful next step is to turn remembered context into work: notice what is due, know which project is in flight, plan, act through tools, delegate, verify, and report evidence. niucode now exposes the primitives for that work: the library target, TurnHooks, the TUI, /plan, /goal, subagents, skills, and the session-scoped extension host.

At the same time, "more powerful" cannot mean "a second framework". The product boundary remains: niucode owns loop, tools, providers, sandbox, and the event log; niuse owns identity, memory, product defaults, and the way work is framed for one person.

Decision

  1. The product is a working companion. Memory is the substrate, not the deliverable. niuse may add project awareness, startup briefs, long-horizon goals, planning, delegation, and evidence capture when they make the companion more useful in real work.

  2. Generic capability goes upstream first. A better loop, goal evaluator, subagent, provider, tool, permission model, or connector belongs in niucode and is consumed through the pinned API. niuse adds only personal semantics and product UX. It never forks kernel files.

  3. Terminal-first, no daemon by default. Proactivity happens at session start, session end, and explicit commands. Background scheduling, push notifications, or a resident service require a later ADR with a concrete need; "always on" is not a default.

  4. Markdown and the event log stay the only durable truth. No database, no vector index, no second session store. Derived views are rebuilt, not persisted as authority.

  5. Safety is part of the capability. Approvals, sandbox policy, secret scanning, and least privilege apply to every new tool, connector, and delegated agent. A capability that cannot be bounded is not shipped.

  6. Every phase needs proof. A phase exits on offline tests plus real use: a dogfood record, a cited past judgement, a completed goal, or a measured regression. A feature that only demos is not done.

Consequences

Better

  • The product can grow from "remembers" to "gets work done" without changing the kernel's identity.
  • Existing niucode work (TUI, goals, subagents, skills) becomes reachable to the person instead of being rebuilt in niuse.
  • The roadmap has explicit exits, so a long-running effort cannot drift into collecting features.

Worse

  • The surface area grows and needs product judgement, not just code.
  • More of niuse's value depends on the pinned niucode revision and its contract tests.
  • Dogfood and evaluation become more important, because autonomy failures are worse than memory failures.

Alternatives

  • Stay memory-only. Rejected: it cannot use what it remembers, and every task still starts from zero.
  • Put personal semantics in niucode. Rejected: it changes what the kernel is and couples two release cadences (ADR-0003).
  • Daemon-first companion. Rejected for now: an operations project with a larger privacy surface, before the terminal loop is proven.
  • Adopt MCP and connectors immediately. Deferred to M8: first make the existing harness usable end to end, then add external capability behind a trust boundary.
docs.excerpt: niuse stays terminal-first and file-based, but grows project awareness, proactive briefs, long-horizon goals, and delegation. Generic capabilities land in niucode first.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Goals are a sixth Markdown store
docs.summary: User outcomes get their own human-owned goals.md, injected after user and before memory; loops stay agent promises and goals never use progress percentages.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-22. Extends the store list in plan §3.1 and the six-store layout in architecture.

Context

loops.md records what the companion promised to do. It is written automatically when the model says it will follow up, and it is about the companion's obligations. A user outcome such as "ship the personal-agent roadmap this month" is a different thing: the human owns it, it spans sessions and projects, and the companion should arrange work around it without silently completing or rewriting it.

niucode's /goal is a session completion condition stored in the session event log. It survives resume, but it does not survive a new thread and is not a product-level intention. Reusing it would make a new chapter forget what the human is trying to achieve.

The alternative of adding goals to user.md would force niuse to edit a human-owned profile automatically, which breaks the ownership rule.

Decision

  1. A sixth store. ~/.niuse/goals.md, same 0700/0600 rules and atomic writes as the other stores.
  2. Human-owned. Only niuse goals add|done and /goals change goals. The model may read them but may not propose, complete, or rewrite them.
  3. Bounded. At most seven open goals; adding beyond that is refused until one is completed or removed by hand.
  4. Injected after user and before memory, budget 300 tokens. The section says explicitly that goals are maintained by the user.
  5. No deadlines and no progress percentages. Deadlines belong to loops.md; percentages turn a companion into a task tracker. A goal is one sentence with an id, a creation date, and an open/done mark.
  6. Secrets are refused at the write, because goals are injected every turn.

Consequences

Better

  • Long-horizon work survives a new thread, a new project, and a restart.
  • The human/agent ownership boundary is visible in the file header and prompt.
  • The store stays readable, reviewable, and cheap to inject.

Worse

  • A seventh prose file to maintain and back up.
  • Users who want sub-tasks or estimates will outgrow it; that is a signal to write a project plan, not to grow this store.

Alternatives

  • Reuse loops.md. Rejected: mixed ownership and two lifecycles in one file.
  • Reuse niucode's session /goal. Rejected: it does not survive a new thread and belongs to the kernel's session state.
  • Auto-update user.md. Rejected: it violates the human-owned profile.
  • A task tracker with progress. Rejected: scope creep and prompt bloat.
docs.excerpt: User outcomes get their own human-owned goals.md, injected after user and before memory; loops stay agent promises and goals never use progress percentages.

docs.title: ADR-0007: thread.jsonl is the only active line
docs.summary: /resume and /fork switch the live session, but thread.jsonl remains the active relationship line across restarts; no pointer file or archive promotion.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-22. Clarifies the thread model in architecture §turn flow and the TUI session commands.

Context

~/.niuse/thread.jsonl is the active relationship line. threads/*.jsonl are archived chapters. The TUI /resume and /fork commands replace the live session for the current run, and since niucode's new-session seam they also notify the embedder hooks. After exit, the next niuse resumes thread.jsonl, not the resumed chapter.

Two alternatives were considered:

  • Pointer file. ~/.niuse/active names the active path. All readers (brief, threads, export, stats) would need to honor it; a stale pointer is a new failure mode and a second index.
  • Promotion. Move the resumed chapter to thread.jsonl and archive the current line. This rewrites the archive identity, breaks open handles and external references, and turns "resume a chapter" into "replace the relationship line".

Decision

  1. thread.jsonl is the only active line across restarts. There is no pointer file and no promotion.
  2. /resume and /fork are session-scoped views. They switch the live session and update in-process hooks; they do not change which file the next launch opens.
  3. /new and /reset archive the current active line and start a new thread.jsonl; this is the only operation that changes the active line across restarts.
  4. Commands that read or write "the thread" must use the live session path, not a cached thread.jsonl, while the TUI is running.
  5. If a user wants a chapter to become the main line, they must do it explicitly by exporting it or moving files by hand; niuse will not silently rewrite the archive.

Consequences

Better

  • One active file, no pointer to go stale.
  • Archived chapters keep their identity and path.
  • /resume is predictable: a view for this session, not a permanent switch.

Worse

  • A resumed chapter is not the next launch's starting point.
  • Users who think of /resume as "open this conversation" may be surprised; the status and help must say "for this session".

Alternatives

  • Pointer file. Rejected: second index and stale-pointer failure mode.
  • Promotion by moving the chapter. Rejected: mutates archive identity and breaks open handles.
  • Make /new a pointer update. Rejected: thread.jsonl already has a clear physical meaning, and M5-004's seam now preserves it.

Follow-up

The TUI help/status should call /resume session-scoped; no code change is required for this decision. M5-006 proves the in-session pointer. Cross-restart promotion is explicitly out of scope.

docs.body_html:
Policy

  • niuse pins niucode in niucode.rev; required CI and Pages check out exactly that commit.
  • The pin moves at most once a week, through scripts/sync-niucode.sh.
  • A nightly workflow runs the same tests against niucode main. Failures are an early signal, not a pull-request gate.
  • scripts/check-niucode-drift.sh reports when the local sibling checkout no longer matches the pin.

The front-end seam is proposed upstream in ADR-0032; this document tracks the call surface niuse uses today.

The contract is deliberately small: run_with_history, AgentConfig, project_history, SessionLog and Event, the provider trait, credentials, sandbox and approval types, per-turn working_dir on one session, and approval denial carrying a structured preview. crates/niuse-cli/tests/niucode_contract.rs exercises them offline with ScriptedProvider, so the check costs no tokens.

One read-only exception: niuse projects reads niucode's workspace metadata at ~/.niucode/projects/*/project.toml (schema 1: cwd, last_seen) and counts sessions/*.jsonl. This is a display view, not a second index; if niucode changes the layout, update crates/niuse-cli/src/projects.rs and its test.

All niuse paths mount niucode's read-only MCP host: niuse tui inherits it, and the REPL/exec call niucode-mcp::McpHost through driver::mount_mcp from NIUSE_MCP_CONFIG or ~/.niucode/mcp.toml. A broken manifest disables MCP for that run with a warning.

docs.body_html:
Stage report · 2026-10-23

This is the checkpoint for the five-round close (75–79). It records what is proven, what is still a gate, and what needs a human decision.

Shipped and verified

  • Harness. niucode has a read-only stdio MCP client, session hooks for embedders, and a new-session path seam. /new, /reset, /resume, and /fork all notify the embedder and are covered by PTY tests.
  • Companion. niuse has seven Markdown stores, goals/plan/evidence/verify, a 10/10-reviewed opt-in digest, and a TUI that records turn metrics. The shared TUI now renders inline Markdown and pipe tables.
  • MCP. niucode-mcp 0.1.5 is published (2026-10-23). ADR-0034 is accepted and niucode ab50b75 implements the write path; niuse exposes --allow-mcp-write, ships an opt-in notes create_note, and the TUI PTY proves the approval preview plus deny/allow (M8 done).
  • Tests. ./scripts/check.sh and ./scripts/eval.sh pass; the TUI suite covers approvals, session isolation, resume/fork pointers, memory prompts, and brief/report/steps composition.
  • Board. 165 cards and 19 docs are generated and link-checked.
  • CI. niucode 2b278fe and niuse ed54d6f are green. niuse c4282f3 passes local check.sh/eval.sh; GitHub CI is pending on a runner backlog, with no red run.

Real evidence

  • 2026-10-22: real exec, notes MCP, TUI, approved write, memory A/B, RSS disagreement, ten digest reviews.
  • 2026-10-23: real TUI tasks read DAY_TWO*.md; the missing TUI on_turn_end was found and fixed, and the first metrics-backed TUI turn was recorded. A real model also called the notes create_note write tool with approval and created stage-write-home.md. The published 0.1.12 binary passed a TUI smoke test and a write-MCP smoke test.
  • Dogfood: 2/10 days, acceptance 100% (1/1), 3 distinct cited memory ids (m-f356, m-5c68, m-3d0b), 1 disagreement.

docs.title: Release 0.1.12
docs.summary: Published 2026-10-23: niuse-core 0.1.12 and niuse 0.1.12 are on crates.io; clean-root install verified.
docs.body_html:
Status

Published · 2026-10-23. niuse-core 0.1.12 and niuse 0.1.12 are on crates.io, and a clean-root install reports niuse 0.1.12. This page records the preflight and the exact order; it is history, not a pending action.

Why 0.1.12

niuse-core 0.1.11 on crates.io predates PlanStep and compose_with_plan, so cargo package -p niuse fails when it resolves the registry core. The workspace is bumped to 0.1.12. niucode-mcp 0.1.5 is already published.

Release result

  • cargo search niuse → 0.1.12
  • cargo install niuse --version 0.1.12 --locked --root /tmp/niuse-0.1.12 installed the binary; niuse --version → niuse 0.1.12
  • The first CLI upload failed verification: pack scripts sat outside the crate and registry niucode 0.1.5 predated EmbedderTool. The fix embeds the packs under crates/niuse-cli/assets and ships niucode 0.1.6.
  • niuse-core 0.1.12 was already uploaded on the first attempt; the retry skipped it and published only the CLI.

Preflight (verified read-only, before the first upload)

  • ./scripts/check.sh passes.
  • cargo package -p niuse-core passes.
  • cargo publish -p niuse-core --dry-run reaches the upload step and aborts at the dry-run warning.
  • ./scripts/publish-niuse.sh --check reports version 0.1.12, the license, and a credentials file.
  • ./scripts/dogfood-trend.sh returns insufficient data (2 active days), not a regression; the publish script treats that as non-blocking.

Commands

Requires explicit human authorization and a clean tree:

cd /home/galbot/Projects/niuverse/niuse
./scripts/publish-niuse.sh --execute

The script:

  1. refuses a dirty tree or a missing token;
  2. runs the dogfood trend and refuses a regression;
  3. publishes niuse-core, waits 20s for the sparse index;
  4. publishes niuse;
  5. skips a crate whose version is already on the index, so a partial run can be retried.

Verify after upload

cargo search niuse-core --limit 1
cargo search niuse --limit 1
cargo package -p niuse
cargo install niuse --version 0.1.12 --locked --root /tmp/niuse-0.1.12
/tmp/niuse-0.1.12/bin/niuse --version

Then update M3-006, M3-001, distribution, and status from “prepared” to the published version.

If it fails

  • Do not reuse 0.1.12 after a failed upload; bump to 0.1.13.
  • A partial run is safe to retry: already-published crates are skipped.
  • A bad release is yanked, not deleted: cargo yank --version 0.1.12 <crate>, then ship the next patch.

docs.title: Dogfood log
docs.summary: Ten-day protocol: one row per day, numbers from stats --json, plus one concrete memory win or disagreement.
docs.body_html:
Why

M2-001 is a product acceptance gate, not a coding task. It needs ten days of real use, recorded while the context is fresh. The record is deliberately small: one row per day, two numbers, one sentence.

Daily ritual (two minutes)

niuse stats --days 1 --json

Append one row below. proposed / accepted come from the JSON; note is a concrete memory win, a disagreement, or -. Do not reconstruct a missed day later; a gap is honest data.

Or record it from the repo root:

niuse dogfood --file docs/dogfood.md --note "one concrete memory win, disagreement, or -"
# or the wrapper: ./scripts/dogfood.sh "note"

niuse dogfood reads today's turn / propose / accept metrics, replaces an existing row for the same date, and only writes a new file private. It refuses to write what looks like a secret. The wrapper calls the binary so there is one implementation of the table update.

The script runs niuse stats --days 1 --json, uses the local calendar date, and inserts or replaces today's row in this table. Run it at the end of a real working day, not to fill a gap.

niuse doctor also reports dogfood: N active day(s) from the turn metrics. That is a convenience counter, not acceptance: only the rows and notes below can close M2.

./scripts/dogfood-check.sh validates this table: dates, counts, duplicates, future days, and the ten-day/60%/three-citations/one-disagreement criteria. Without --complete it only reports gaps; with --complete it exits non-zero until every criterion holds. The citations and disagreement counts are text heuristics, so a human still reviews the notes.

dateturnsproposedacceptednote
2026-10-221911real exec/MCP/TUI/write; A/B cited m-3d0b; disagreement dropped RSS; 10/10 digests, M6 closed; M5 TUI day 1/10
2026-10-23400published 0.1.12 TUI + write MCP smoke; TEST_ANYTIME_OK cited m-f356 m-5c68 m-3d0b; 4 turns

Rules

  • A "memory win" means it cited a past judgement and saved a round of explanation, or avoided a repeated mistake. Name the entry id if possible.
  • A "disagreement" means it pushed back and you changed your mind. Record what changed.
  • If acceptance is zero for several days, stop and inspect the candidates instead of pushing through. Noise is a product bug.
  • Keep the store under 50 entries. If it grows faster, the proposal bar is too low.

Weekly check

niuse stats --days 7 --trend

Look for the direction, not the absolute number: acceptance should rise as the store matures, and the notes should become more specific.

scripts/dogfood-trend.sh automates the look: it compares the last seven active days with the previous seven and fails when acceptance drops by more than 20 points (once both windows have at least three active days and five proposals). --strict also fails on a token-per-turn blow-up or a shrinking day count. scripts/publish-niuse.sh runs it before publishing and refuses on a regression.

Done

Ten rows, acceptance at or above 60%, at least three cited judgements, at least one recorded disagreement. Then M2-001 can move to review, and the next milestone is decided from the notes rather than from the backlog.

Self-check (does not count as a day)

2026-10-22 · synthetic write task in a scratch repo, --sandbox workspace-write --approval ask.

  • The approval preview showed the expected one-line diff, y approved the write, and the file changed.
  • Found: usage printed once per model step, so one prompt produced four usage lines; /cost counted steps as turns. Fixed in M2-053; a run now prints one N steps · … line and /cost reports 1 turn.
  • Found: --approval ask also prompts for read-only tools such as bash cat; the model recovered by using read. Not a bug, but the transcript makes the extra approval visible.
  • /export wrote a 0600 Markdown file from the live REPL; /stats matched the one run.

A second self-check the same day covered two writes with the second approval denied: a.txt changed, b.txt stayed untouched, and the model reported the partial result. A scripted $EDITOR also exercised mem review → e: the text changed, the confirmation date refreshed, and mem_review_edit landed in metrics.jsonl.

A crafted offline inbox exercised niuse review without a provider: y accepted one candidate, n discarded the other, the inbox was rewritten empty, and metrics.jsonl recorded review_accept / review_discard.

A fourth self-check chose k at the conflict prompt: both lessons remained, and metrics.jsonl recorded keep:<id>. A real bootstrap over two short niucode sessions extracted zero candidates, which is plausible for 375- and 2.1k-char sessions; the tool correctly left the inbox empty. A later --profile-only over three sessions wrote a user.md draft and explicitly said there was no evidence for red lines instead of inventing them.

A third self-check used two sessions on a fresh home: the second session's banner showed the memory injected, a contradictory lesson triggered the [r] 替换 / [k] 并存 / [d] 丢弃 prompt with the old text quoted, and r left exactly one entry. stats counted 2 proposals / 2 accepted; /cost across the resumed thread reported 2 turns.

A sixth REPL check went /new → /resume 2 → /new: the stale active log was archived instead of reopened, and two archives in the same millisecond got a -1 suffix instead of overwriting each other.

A fifth, provider-free REPL check exercised /new, numbered /threads, /resume 2, and /cost: the archive moved to slot 2, resume switched the active marker, and /cost reported the archived thread's 2 turns from its own log.

This is a smoke test of the loop, not evidence about usefulness. The ten real days are still the gate.

docs.title: Offline personal-agent evals
docs.summary: Named offline cases for memory injection, goal lifecycle, the startup brief, and the notes MCP pack. A prompt/turn regression suite, not a model benchmark.
docs.body_html:
Run

./scripts/eval.sh

The script runs the Rust cases with cargo test, the notes-pack MCP integration, and (when the sibling checkout exists) niucode's MCP client and agent-dispatch tests. No API key, network, or model call is involved.

Cases

CaseWhat it proves

reports_files_checks_failures_and_denialsIncludes a completed delegation's task and summary
an_unfinished_delegation_is_not_reported_as_successA spawn without a result is ?, not ✓
report_json_combines_metrics_stores_and_dogfoodOne read-only weekly review covers cost, stores, and the log
dogfood_writes_and_replaces_todays_row_from_metricsThe daily row comes from metrics; same-day rerun replaces

pty_memory_discard_does_not_store_the_candidateDiscard leaves the store unchanged

pty_resume_moves_hooks_to_the_resumed_session/resume moves hooks; /verify lands in the resumed log

pty_tui_closes_a_step_only_after_tagged_verificationThe full TUI plan/verify flow works in a terminal

a_failed_verification_keeps_the_step_open_until_a_passFailure stays visible, blocks done, then a pass closes it

mcp_init_merges_new_servers_and_keeps_existing_textA new pack is appended; comments survive; invalid TOML is untouched
mcp_init_writes_a_mountable_read_only_configGenerated config mounts and both packs answer
calendar_pack_lists_and_searches_without_networkA second read-only pack lists, searches, and excludes out-of-window events
stats_json_reports_cache_hit_and_tokens_per_turnCost signals are derived from token totals, not guessed
volatile_sections_do_not_change_the_cacheable_prefixDate, promises, and journal stay out of the cache prefix
a_fat_store_stays_under_the_prompt_budgetA 200-memory store stays under 4.2k tokens
plan_injection_caps_at_six_stepsA 50-step plan injects six, not all
memory_is_truncated_before_it_can_dominate_the_prompt500 memories are dropped, not appended
plan_prompt_injects_open_steps_and_skips_done_onesOpen steps reach the prompt; done steps do not
plan_steps_close_only_after_step_verificationA step is refused until verify --step passes, then closes and shows in evidence
verify_records_and_evidence_reports_itA passing and a failing niuse verify append events and appear in evidence
evidence_json_reports_files_and_checksA thread's write path, check, and failure are reported as JSON
a_turn_can_call_memory_searchThe model calls memory_search and receives both fresh and expired memory with ids
notes_pack_searches_reads_and_refuses_escapeA real MCP pack searches, reads, and rejects a path escape
a_hung_tool_times_out_and_kills_the_serverA hung MCP server cannot stall the session
a_writable_server_is_refused_before_spawnA non-read-only manifest never starts

Each case is named for the capability, so a red test says what regressed instead of only which file changed.

What this is not

  • It does not measure model quality; the provider is scripted.
  • It does not cover token cost or latency.
  • It does not replace dogfood. Real use still decides whether the companion is useful; these cases keep the plumbing honest between dogfood days.

Next cases

  • A dogfood trend check that blocks a release when acceptance or token trends regress. This needs real days, not a scripted provider.
