docs.title: Distribution notes
docs.summary: A two-checkout build works; cargo install --git and crates.io do not, because niucode's path dependencies sit outside this repository. The dependency strategy and license are still open.
docs.body_html:
What works today

niuse builds from a workspace containing both checkouts at the expected relative paths:

workspace/
  niuse/          this repository
  niucode/        the pinned checkout

git clone https://github.com/niuverse/niuse
git clone https://github.com/niuverse/niucode
cd niuse
cargo build --release
# or install the binary from the checkout
cargo install --path crates/niuse-cli --locked

Verified on 2026-10-22: cargo install --path crates/niuse-cli --root /tmp/niuse-install --locked --debug produced a working niuse 0.1.0.

Why cargo install --git does not work

cargo install --git https://github.com/niuverse/niuse clones only niuse. The dependencies niucode-agent, niucode-core, and the other niucode-* crates are declared as path = "../niucode/crates/...", so a clean clone has no such directory and Cargo cannot fetch it.

Verified on 2026-10-22 by cloning the repository into /tmp and running cargo metadata:

error: failed to load manifest for workspace member `.../crates/niuse-cli`
Caused by: failed to load manifest for dependency `niucode-agent`

The README quick start therefore requires a local checkout of ../niucode; that requirement is real, not a temporary convenience.

Why crates.io is blocked

cargo package -p niuse fails:

error: all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging.
dependency `niucode-agent` does not specify a version

crates.io removes path specifications and expects the dependency to exist in the registry. Until that changes, only niuse-core is packageable on its own, and it is not useful without the CLI.

Chosen path (2026-10-22)

Publish the niucode-* crates first at 0.1.0, then consume them by version. The path dependencies in niuse already carry version = "0.1.0" beside path, so local development keeps the sibling checkout while packaging can resolve registry versions once the upload exists.

Current state (2026-10-23): niuse and niuse-core are published at 0.1.12; the eight niucode-* crates, including niucode-mcp, are published at 0.1.6. cargo package -p niuse passes against the registry, and a clean-root cargo install niuse --version 0.1.12 --locked reports niuse 0.1.12.

The 0.1.11 core predated the plan API, and 0.1.5 predated EmbedderTool; those were version-discipline bugs. The fix is the coordinated 0.1.12/0.1.6 release. Pack servers are embedded under crates/niuse-cli/assets so cargo package can build them; scripts/check-pack-assets.sh keeps the copies identical.

Options

OptionCostWhen
Publish the niucode-* crates first, then depend on versionsRelease coordination between the two repositoriesAfter niucode's embedding surface stabilizes
Convert the dependency spec to git with a pinned revisionEvery clean build fetches from GitHub; local co-development needs [patch] overridesIf clean-checkout installs matter before publishing
Keep the two-checkout buildNo crates.io presence, no docs.rs page, no one-command installAcceptable while the tool is personal

A cargo install --git line is not among the options: it cannot resolve the path dependencies. Switching to git dependencies is a different change; it edits Cargo.toml and keeps the pin in the revision.

The pinned-revision policy in compat is independent of this choice; it keeps the required CI reproducible either way.

Names

niuse, niuse-core, niuse-cli, and niucode were unclaimed on crates.io, npm, and PyPI when checked on 2026-10-21. Recheck immediately before publishing; registry names are first-come. The binary name is independent of the crate name, so a rename is recoverable.

License

MIT OR Apache-2.0, the usual Rust dual license. LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE are at the repository root and license.workspace is inherited by every crate. crates.io can now accept the packages.

Checklist

  • Choose a license and add it to the workspace manifest.
  • Choose publishing the niucode crates first at 0.1.0; until the upload exists, clean-checkout installs still need the sibling checkout.
  • Add CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN / cargo login and run the release workflow.
  • Recheck crate names and reserve them with a real release.
  • Add a release workflow that runs scripts/check.sh before publish.

docs.title: Renderer migration
docs.summary: What niuse's renderer does, which hooks exist, and why the files do not move until confirmation and command seams land.
docs.body_html:
Renderer migration

Status: gap analysis, 2026-10-22. No renderer code has moved yet.

What exists

  • niuse owns a small renderer: crates/niuse-cli/src/render.rs (361 lines) plus the REPL loop in repl.rs. It does five jobs:
    • streaming text through candidate::StreamFilter, which strips <<niuse:*>> blocks;
    • parsing the stripped answer into memory / loop / journal candidates;
    • rendering tool calls, tool results, warnings, compaction, and one usage line;
    • asking y/n/e/s for a candidate and r/k/d for a conflict;
    • approval previews with a unified diff, 80-line cap, and d for the full diff.
  • niucode owns the TUI: tui.rs (2 774), terminal.rs (480), live.rs (460), and presentation.rs (246). It owns the alternate screen, inline viewport, composer, history, approvals, diff rendering, markdown-ish theme, details view, and slash commands.

The duplication is real, but it is not one renderer: niuse's candidate confirmation and memory commands are product UI, not terminal plumbing.

Seams now available (niucode 0.1.5+)

  • run_tui_with_hooks(TuiOptions, Box<dyn TurnHooks>).
  • augment_system_prompt — memory/identity injection.
  • on_event — observe every runtime AgentEvent.
  • filter_text — mutate a text delta before display; the persisted event is untouched.
  • on_turn_end — observe the final RunOutcome.
  • after_turn / on_answer — ask a numbered question after a successful turn; the host renders it and returns the choice.

filter_text (published in niucode 0.1.3) is the first renderer seam: a niuse hook can run StreamFilter and strip protocol blocks before the TUI prints them, while capturing the raw deltas for parsing at turn end. The example hooked_tui.rs verifies the filter under a PTY.

Gaps that still block deleting render.rs

  1. Candidate confirmation. after_turn provides a generic numbered prompt, and the tui feature carries CompanionHooks (capture, parse, auto loop/journal, memory accept/discard). niuse tui wires it end to end, including conflict replace/keep and e edit. Read-only /mem, /loops, /journal, /status, /cost, /threads, /sessions, /export, /prompt, /identity, and /user work through the command hook and are registered in help/completion; automatic journal/loop writes also record metrics. The TUI's per-turn usage line keeps niucode's shape; /cost reads the same thread event log as the REPL.
  2. Product commands. TurnHooks::commands and TurnHooks::command now register and dispatch product commands; /brief, /mem, /loops, /journal, /status, /cost, /export, /threads, /sessions, /prompt, /identity, and /user are reachable from the TUI.
  3. Approval presentation. The TUI pager renders a scrollable full-screen diff, and niucode 2d12360 lets an embedder configure the approval keys; niuse sets y/n/s, so d no longer denies. tests/tui_approval.py proves deny/allow and that d is ignored. The 80-line cap is a REPL property; the pager scrolls instead of truncating.
  4. Usage and /cost. /cost now reads the thread event log, so it agrees with the REPL and the log by construction. The per-turn line remains niucode's turn N · in · out · cache% shape.
  5. Config semantics. TuiOptions is close to niuse's CLI flags, but niuse's config precedence, NIUSE_MEMORY=off, and provider presets still live in niuse.

Staged plan

  1. Text filter (done). filter_text exists and is verified; niuse can strip protocol blocks while capturing raw text.
  2. Post-turn interaction hook (next). Add a hook that lets the embedder present a candidate decision through the host UI, or a first-class "candidate" widget/command extension. This is the hard one.
  3. Command registry injection. Let the embedder add slash commands with help text and completion.
  4. Opt-in TUI mode (prototype done). niuse tui runs under the tui feature with CompanionHooks; a replay PTY test confirms protocol stripping, the accept/discard question, and the memory write. The rustyline REPL remains the default.
  5. Retire render.rs only after ten real dogfood days on the TUI path, the same bar as M2. Until then the renderer stays; it is not dead code.

Decision

Do not migrate the renderer by moving files. Extend the hook surface first: a post-turn interaction seam and command registration are cheaper and safer than porting candidate UI into niucode. The two repos stay separate (ADR-0003).

The cost today is one small renderer; the cost of a premature migration is a product UI split across two event loops.

docs.title: Dashboard guide
docs.summary: Sources, generation commands, the four views, and the ritual for adding modules, cards, and docs.
docs.body_html:
What this is

docs/index.html is the project's only architecture reading surface: Architecture, Work, Docs, and Decisions share one three-column shell. It is generated from repository sources, opens offline, and needs no server.

cargo xtask dashboard          # writes docs/index.html and docs/dashboard/model.json
cargo xtask dashboard --check  # CI: fails when generated output is stale or references break

Generation is deterministic: the same inputs produce the same HTML. receipt.json records the build time, git revision, and input list, but is not part of the staleness check.

Four views

  • Architecture (default): modules by layer, dependency arrows, contracts, and source. Selecting a module focuses its relations; status only shows implementation state, not progress.
  • Work: one file per card, a handoff surface filtered by milestone. No completion rates, WIP counts, or progress bars.
  • Docs: a Markdown index with a reading pane; supports deep links such as #/docs/adr-0001.
  • Decisions: ADR cards plus a kind = "decision" timeline. Completion logs do not belong here.

Sources

docs/
  index.html                # generated, committed, openable via file://
  dashboard/
    project.json            # project, milestones, layers, modules, relations, decisions
    template.html           # single-file shell
    style.css               # three-column layout and views
    app.js                  # framework-free rendering
    model.json              # generated
    receipt.json            # build receipt, gitignored
  board/
    M0-001-five-stores.md   # one card per file
  adr/
    0001-memory-layer.md
    0002-identity-layer.md
    0003-kernel-product-boundary.md
  architecture.md
  compat.md
  plan.md
  status.md
  distribution.md
  dogfood.md

Adding things

Add a module: add an entry to modules in project.json. Its layer must exist and paths must point at real files; any module not marked planned needs at least one existing path.

Add a work card: create a Markdown file under docs/board/. The TOML frontmatter must include id, title, status, milestone, size, and updated; done requires completed, and blocked requires blocked_reason.

Add a doc: any .md under docs/ with TOML frontmatter between +++ lines, including at least id, title, and kind. ADR status accepts only proposed, accepted, superseded, rejected, or draft.

Add a decision: write an ADR, or add a kind = "decision" event to project.json. When doing both, link them with refs.

Discipline

Run ./scripts/check.sh before committing; it covers fmt, clippy, docs, tests, package, and dashboard freshness.

The board is read-only; the browser cannot write back. State changes go through the repository, so the board never becomes a second source of truth. Run --check before committing.

events.title: Position niuse as cross-project engineering memory
events.detail: Not a general agent, not a second brain. Only preferences, decisions, and pitfalls; project knowledge stays in AGENTS.md.

events.title: Keep the identity layer separate from memory
events.detail: identity is human-written and the agent may only propose; journal and loops are automatic; memory requires confirmation. What persists is the identity, not a process.

events.title: Emit protocol blocks in-band from the main model
events.detail: No extra model call. Missing a memory is acceptable; recording a wrong one is not. Streaming needs a tail buffer.

events.title: MVP implemented
events.detail: Five stores, prompt, protocol, REPL, driver, and bootstrap landed; the offline test suite passes.

events.title: Reuse niucode's architecture-first board
events.detail: Same xtask generator and three-column shell, with a niuse project model. The board records architecture and implementation, not runtime monitoring.

events.title: Keep two repos and move the front end upstream
events.detail: niucode owns the kernel, TUI, and hooks; niuse owns identity, memory, policy, and defaults. Merge only if the product layer becomes thin enough that separate releases stop mattering.

events.title: Grow from memory layer to working companion
events.detail: niuse adds project context, briefs, goals, and delegation while generic capability lands in niucode first. No daemon, no second store; every phase exits on real use.

events.title: Give human goals their own store
events.detail: goals.md is human-owned, injected after user and before memory, and capped at seven open goals; loops remain the companion's promises.

events.title: Keep thread.jsonl as the only active line
events.detail: TUI /resume and /fork switch the live session and notify hooks, but do not change the next launch. No pointer file, no archive promotion; /new and /reset are the only cross-restart switches.
